articleTitle: Robust sensor faults observer design for continuous-time switched systems using descriptor approach
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper considers the problem of designing a robust descriptor observer for simultaneous state and sensor faults estimation of continuous-time switched linear systems in the presence of unknown external disturbances. An augmented singular switched system is constructed from the original switched systems by considering the sensor faults term as a part of a new extended state vector. Stability conditions are established and formulated into H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performances by minimizing the effect of external disturbance from the residual and a Lyapunov stability theory is utilized for switched system stability combined with the Average Dwell Time (ADT) concept. The observer parameter matrices are also determined by solving a convex optimization problem under Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMI) constraints. Finally, a numerical example and a Highly MAneuverable Technology (HiMAT) vehicle are investigated to prove the efficacy of the obtained results.

articleTitle: Multi-objective FSC-MPC for single phase three level grid connected F-Type inverter PEMFC system
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The application of model predictive control (MPC) in energy conversion systems has lately attracted a lot of attention, both theoretically and experimentally. To control multi-level inverters in grid-connected operations, different MPC algorithms have been proposed, enabling great performance and quick dynamic responsiveness.The architecture and study of a single three-level grid-connected F-type inverter PEMFC system are presented in this study. A proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) is used as an energy producing unit, and the system is connected to the grid through a DC-DC converter and a DC-AC inverter built with the MATLAB-Simulink tool box. To extract the maximum power from the PEMFC we link it with BOOST converte and we apply fuzzy logic (MPPT) during rapid temperature changes. The second part is the inverter which is controlled by a proposed Multi-objective FSC-MPC to ensure excellent ac power quality on the grid side. It is important to provide great tracking effects and robustness. The simulation results show that the proposed method not only completely eliminates or minimizes (THD) of alternating current and also keeps its sinusoidal form with less fluctuation.

articleTitle: Fuzzy adaptive backstepping for the control of the electrical drive wheels' speed
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents a new speed control technique for a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) in an electric vehicle based on a new nonlinear backstepping technique. To regulate the electric car's speed and torque, we designed a non-adaptive speed controller for a permanent magnet synchronous motor. Our propulsion system consists of two synchronous permanent magnet motors. The various static error constants are modified in accordance with the speed error using the fuzzy adaptive backstepping controller.Fuzzy direct torque control is the foundation of the proposed model (FDTC). The rules are first modified using the stator's current membership functions, and then a fuzzy direct torque controller of the Mamdani type is created. The electronic differential does the calculations, enabling independent control of each driving wheel in any curve.The Matlab/Simulink program is used to conduct modeling and simulation in order to examine the effectiveness of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Synthesis of TPU/MWCNT Nanocomposite-Based Filament for Strain Sensors Application
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: There is a huge demand for flexible strain sensors due to the rapid development of wearable devices. Nevertheless, conventional metals and rigid semiconductor-based strain sensors have been limited in their application due to their poor stretchability and sensitivity, and a great deal of effort has been put into finding suitable sensors to overcome these limitations. Filament-based strain sensors are a new technology that can be used to make wearable electronic devices. Due to their intrinsic properties, filament-based sensors are superior to conventional rigid sensors for detecting human body motions due to their weight, flexibility, stitchability, and especially their high stretchability. In this paper, multiwalled carbon nanotubes and thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU/MWCNT) were combined using mechanical force methods to produce dispersions of MWCNT with different types of TPU. Different types of filaments were fabricated using an easy and cost-effective method, which is extrusion. Moreover, the effect of the nature of the TPU on the stability of the sensors’ conductivities is investigated. The performances of these filaments were analyzed in terms of mechanical, electrical, and electromechanical properties. The results show that the sensor with the combination of TPU<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/MWCNT exhibits a strong capacity to transform mechanical deformation into an electrical response. The elastic zone was estimated at 24.49% (linearity = 0.98 within the elastic zone) and 10.1 MPa of young modulus.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of a Compact SSRR for Passive RFID Tag Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, a small long read range tag antenna based on single split sing-resonator is proposed. This new structure consists of two elements, one acting as a radiating body of the SSRR part which is represented in the outer ring and the other as a broadside coupling part which is represented by interdigital tracks. The antenna miniaturization is achieved by embedding the interdigital tracks inside the SSRR. This technique lengthens the current path and in consequence reduces the antenna size. The proposed tag which is simulated using CST Microwave Studio has a compact size of 20 × 20 × 0.49 mm3 with the peak read range is greater than 9m at UHF European band (865-868MHz). This tag has the advantages of low cost, small size, lightweight, and simple to design. The new approach could be used in RFID application which requires a compact size antenna.

articleTitle: Simple and Robust Control Algorithm for Three Phases Hybrid Excitation Synchronous Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: this paper is present a simple control strategy of a synchronous motor with hybrid excitation based on excitation current regulation. This control technique makes it possible to impose approximately constant stator currents irrespective of the speed and the resistive torque of the vehicle. The designer has the choice of regulating these currents relative to their choice of the reference current. This control technique is possible by regulating the excitation current by a chopper with two quadrants. The regulation of the excitation current causes the regulation of the electric constant of the motor and subsequently the regulation of the electromagnetic torque necessary to drive the vehicle at the desired speed. This control technique allows a significant simplification of the simulation time of the control algorithm with respect to the classical control laws namely: classic scalar control, direct control of the torque (DTC), control by flow orientation and vector control. The control strategy developed is validate following the implementation of the global model under the Matlab-Simulink simulation environment. The results of simulations are with a good scientific level and encourage the industrialization of the global system.

articleTitle: HESG based WECS Overview, modeling, and fractional order control
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this study, we set out to learn more about how a Hybrid Excited Synchronous Generator (HESG) may operate in a Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS). For use with wind energy, this article presents a solid framework for a HESG coupled to an isolated load. Multiple WECS architectures are discussed before the HESG is suggested as a promising replacement for the standard generator. Then, we modeled wind turbines in Matlab/Simulink, accounting for the aerodynamic component (wind), the electrical component (generator and power converters), and the mechanical component (turbine and drive shaft). To achieve our goals, we presented a control strategy with an inside current loop using a PI corrector and an exterior speed loop using a fractional order PI controller.

articleTitle: Adaptive Computation Offloading for Heterogeneous IoT Applications: An Experimental Study
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) applications are heterogeneous in terms of the deployed hardware, developed protocols, and requirements of each of these applications. The decision whether to process such applications at the sensor nodes or at a higher layer (i.e., Edge, Fog, or Cloud) heavily depends on those heterogeneity features. In this paper, we propose a number of adaptive schemes to address the local processing vs. offloading of IoT applications based on their energy consumption and execution time. To this end, we deploy six IoT applications on real sensor nodes, measure their energy consumption and execution time, and then decide where to process the application based on the measurements. We study the performance of the proposed schemes in terms of energy efficiency and execution time. We also compare their performances to selected non-adaptive schemes.

articleTitle: Flooding Attack: Implementation, Detection, and Prevention for UAV
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) use is increasing daily, which results in increasing their security threat landscape. A major security threat to availability for network-based devices is Denial of Service (DoS) and Flooding attacks, which impact the system resources and disturb the network communications. For Mobile Ad hoc Networks (MANETs), there are multiple previous works on DoS attacks implementation and mitigation using different techniques. However, the work is limited for 2D networks with little focus on detecting and mitigating such attacks on 3D networks of Flying AdHoc Networks (FANETs). This study focuses on the RREQ flooding attack on a 3D network of drones and proposes a threshold-based detection and mitigation mechanism that considers the drones limited resources. The simulation experiments demonstrate a 34% throughput improvement and 3% energy saving.

articleTitle: Fuel Consumption Optimization for Parallel Hybrid Vehicle based on Divided Rectangle Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Fuel consumption is one of the most serious environmental problems. Hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) play a very important role in saving energy and reducing emissions. Parallel hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) manage energy between components based on fuzzy logic control strategies. Optimization algorithms determine the characteristics of PHEVs to improve fuel efficiency. Apply the Divided Rectangle Algorithm (DIRECT) to PHEVs to solve specific fuel efficiency optimization problems. The DIRECT algorithm has made it possible to determine the optimal size parameters of the components to increase the efficiency of the PHEV and reduce pollution.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm based Multi-objective optimization of SMPM
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The present work deals with the optimization of an in-wheel surface mounted permanent magnet motor (SMPM) with an outer rotor and concentrated windings. At first, it is necessary to determine the equations dealing with the analytical model. To find the optimum design geometry, two objective functions were used. The first leads to maximize the efficiency of the machine. The second it is to minimize the machine weight. Additionally, the basic principles and concepts of single and multi-objective Genetic Algorithms (GA) are reviewed. Two algorithms, the fast elitist multi-objective Genetic Algorithm (NSGA-II) and the cell model of the genetic algorithm (Mocell) are applied. The results obtained by both algorithms were compared and analyzed.

articleTitle: Wind energy Conversion System Using PMSG Controlled by Vector Control and Nonlinear Backstepping Strategies
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The control domain of nonlinear systems require robust controls to guarantee a level of stability and better performance. This paper treats a nonlinear control of a wind energy conversion system (WECS) based on a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) with maximum power extraction. A nonlinear control strategy proposed is Backstepping control (BSC) based on the Lyapunov approach. The objective of this paper is to target two main objectives via develop linear and non-linear control strategies for a wind energy conversion system based on a direct drive and variable speed. So, the wind energy conversion system (WECS) include both classical control based on PI regulators use for tracking the maximum power point with mechanical speed controller method in order to guarantee the maximum wind power and nonlinear Backstepping control based on Lyapunov theory using in the global scheme of the vector control by replacing the PI regulator by Backstepping regulator.

Author Keywords: Backstepping Control Wind Energy Conversion System

articleTitle: Energy Management in Microgrids with Renewable Energy Sources and Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents a smart scheme for managing power in a grid-connected and island mode microgrid considering loads priority. The proposed system is developed to manage the energy usage between the hybrid resource and the energy storage system to lower electricity bill. This is achieved by supplying the loads with energy generated from the photovoltaic system and energy storage system besides reducing the energy exchange between the main network and the microgrid. The proposed methodology is based on the difference between the available renewable energy generation, the energy required for active loads, the energy storage system, the state of charge, and the electricity market price. The results show that the proposed controller can achieve lower operating cost and reduce power exchange between the main grid and the micro grid.

articleTitle: A calibration methodology of low-cost air pollutant sensor calibration using neural networks
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Air quality Low cost sensors (LCSs) are cheap and can map extensive areas. They alert people about pollution spikes in smart city buildings (schools, universities, hospitals …) or industrial areas. Before using them for a specified task, they must be calibrated to give accurate readings, i.e. they must be aligned with a measure based on a reference machine. Unfortunately, classic calibration is limited by interferences with other pollutants or can be affected by atmosphere constants in the case of uncontrolled environments. This paper proposes a calibration solution based on artificial neural networks (ANN).

articleTitle: High-performance Super twisting sliding mode MPPT control for photovoltaic system under partial shading conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to offer an improved maximum power point tracking (MPPT) approach for photovoltaic (PV) systems using the super-twisting algorithm. The proposed approach has the ability to track the MPP under adverse environmental circumstances such as large fluctuations of insolation and partial shade. In addition, this method minimizes the chattering effect and increases efficiency. The effectiveness of the proposed method is tested under changing solar radiation and compared to conventional sliding mode control and to perturb and observe(P&O) technique. MATLAB/Simulink is used to simulate the PV-MPPT system. The results indicate that the developed method has a better dynamic response than conventional sliding mode control. It can be used in photovoltaic generation systems.

articleTitle: 3D FEA of the Performances of Magnetic Separator for Different Drum Topologies
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The separators performances and process are improved by new recovering technologies based on separation theories, model of force and magnetic field nature. However, numerous electrostatics and magnetics separators generate the electromagnetic field, these separators are classified on the kind of recovered particles: nonmetallic, metallic or nonferrous. The separators development are based on the configuration size and magnetic source based on electromagnet or permanent magnet: intensities, form, number, orientation. In this study, two magnetic separators are proposed with two configuration of drum, the buried magnet drum and the surface magnet drum respectively. The paper aim is to study using the 3D Finite Element Analysis to compare the effectiveness and the performance of the separator in the presence of aluminum particle near the two configuration of separator to show the magnetic effect, induced current and ejection force. The FEA results illustrate the effect of configurations of eddy current separator on separation parameters. These results can help to optimize the size and magnet position of new magnetic separator.

articleTitle: Active and Reactive Power Control of the PMSG based on wind energy conversion system using Nonlinear Backstepping Control
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents a new robust nonlinear control strategy based on backstepping control applied to control active and reactive power for permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) integrated into a wind energy conversion system (WECS). The goal of this control is to achieve high static and dynamic performance in terms of reference tracking, sensitivity to parameter changes, rejection of external disturbances, and reduction of the chattering phenomenon when compared to the traditional sliding mode control strategy. The use of the classic control technique in sliding mode gives quite interesting results, but its main disadvantage lies in the chattering phenomenon (appearance of high frequency oscillations) caused by the discontinuous control signal, which reduces precision and performance of the system. For this, we propose in this paper a technique to eliminate this chattering phenomenon through the use of a Non-Linear robust control based on the backstepping approach. The proposed technique allows having improvable performance while keeping the robustness of the system and the convergence in finite time. Simulation results demonstrate the good effectiveness and excellent robustness of the proposed technique comparatively to the SMC one.

articleTitle: Analysis Model And Numerical Investigation Of Electromagnetic Tube Expansion With Field Concentrator
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Electromagnetic forming EMF is a high-speed forming process that consists of generating a pulsed magnetic field by discharging a capacitor bank through a coil. The interaction of the intense transient magnetic fields between the coil and the workpiece generates high electromagnetic pressure and results in the deformation of the workpiece. Numerical analyses of the EMF process have only recently been undertaken. Previous works concentrated on analyzing the electromagnetic tube expansion and the effect of forming conditions on the process. However, system setup for high-energy electromagnetic forming often includes an additional component which is the magnetic field concentrator placed between the coil and the workpiece. This additional component significantly complicates the analysis of the electromagnetic bulging and the modeling of the system that becomes 3D. This paper summarizes the analysis conducted to show the effect of the field concentrator on tube electromagnetically expanded. To study this effect, in the finite element model improved previously to simulate the magnetic tube expansion, an analytical model, inspired by the Muhlbauer one, has been developed.

articleTitle: Convex Optimization in Model Predictive Control based on Hammerstein Model
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This work deals with Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) based on Hammerstein models. The non-convex optimization problem is converted into a convex one by reducing the control domain. A variety of deterministic gradient based methods including Trust Region (TR) and Interior Point (IP) and stochastic methods such as Nelder-Mead (NM), Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) are discussed and numerically compared in terms of tracking performances and computation times. The NM algorithm offers the less computation time per iteration compared to the above mentioned methods. Furthermore, it offers the best tracking performances. The results are proven through simulations treating a SISO model.

articleTitle: Fractional Order Based Controllers For Lower Limb Exoskeleton In Contact Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper , a three degrees of freedom lower limb exoskeleton is modeled in case of contacting with ground . The dynamic equations for lower limb exoskeleton in reduced order form are derived based on augmented Lagrange equations which include Lagrange multiplier and Jacobian vectors. The controller is constructed using fractional order calculus theory combined with the sliding mode surface to ensure that the control system has strong robust characteristics and fast convergence. A comparative study between a conventional Fractional Order proportional derivative controller (FOPD) and Fractional order sliding mode (FOSMC) has been established. Simulation results have performed by comparing both controllers in the same conditions. The results of simulation indicate that FOSMC has a good tracking performance and an excellent robustness against system uncertainties and external disturbances as compared with Fractional order PD Controller FOPD.

articleTitle: Modeling of p+/n-well and n+/p-well Diodes Based on 1μm CMOS Technology Using GWO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Two different diode configurations—n+/p-well and p+/n-well—are fabricated and characterized according to the standard CMOS 1μm process technology at the Micro-fabrication Technological Platform (PTM) of the Centre de Developpement des Technologies Avancees (CDTA). Current-voltage measurements of the diodes are done for different temperatures, 27, 120, and 160 °C. Using heuristic algorithm, which called Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO), the obtained I-V data were used to extract the main diode electronic parameters, such as ideality factor (n), barrier height (ϕ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>), saturation current (Is) and series resistance (Rs). The extraction stage aims to provide information regarding the devices' enhancement and conduction process. The results confirm the validity of the process design and parameters extraction.

articleTitle: The Effect of Sensor Array Design on Acoustic Imaging for Enhancing HFCWO Therapy
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Innovative therapy with multiple independent actuators in high-frequency chest wall oscillation devices can be facilitated by targeting the detected nidus in the lung for higher therapy efficacy and efficiency. Acoustic imaging allows the detection of the nidus by converting the respiratory acoustic energy distribution to an image. However, the design of acoustic imaging systems, such as the sensor number, sensing diameter, and detectable nidus length has been typically empirical and yet to be examined. Hence, the impact of the sensor number and the sensors sensing diameter on the detectable nidus length via airway remodeling is examined in this study to provide quantitative design guidelines for new and existing acoustic imaging system. The nidus associated with mucus at each airway layer is simulated as localized high airway impedances to study the airway pressure and airflow characteristic through mathematical modeling by combining airway parameters such as, airway length, wall thickness, inner radius, and tissue structure. The nidus can be identified truthfully through the acoustic image output from the airway model. Nidus length resolution range of 73 mm to 4.35 mm via acoustic imaging can be detected with about 4 to 26,000 sensors, and with sensor sensing overlapping area between 0% and 95%. The resolution of the identified nidus length improves with the increase in sensor number.

articleTitle: Fast Supercapacitor Charging for Electromagnetic Converter Systems by Self Powered Boost Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Electromagnetic energy harvesting (EM) is an interesting method for obtaining energy from vibration sources to power autonomous wireless sensor systems. This is reached with the help of energy management circuits that can be based on voltage multipliers circuits or boost rectifier circuits. These energy management structures aim to raise the voltage of the EM converter to a level that is adequate for the storage element. In this paper, a dual-mode AC/DC circuit for EM is proposed for fast charging of the supercapacitor. The circuit is based on a boost rectifier and a voltage multiplier using discrete elements and without a startup circuit. This structure can work properly with an EM converter generating power in the range of a few µW. The circuit can work under different frequencies and accelerations. In the first step, the proposed circuit store the energy in a supercapacitor in voltage multiplier mode until it reaches 1.9 V. After that, the supercapacitor will supply the ancillary circuit to activate the boost mode based on bidirectional MOSFETs, which reduce the time to charge the supercapacitor. The maximum power consumption of the ancillary circuit is 34 µW. The experimental investigation shows that the system at acceleration ACC = 0.17 g and Freq = 27 Hz is able to charge the supercapacitor by a voltage of 5.41 V in 7 min. The proposed solution helps to enhance the time to charge comparing conventional voltage multiplier structure by 23 min.

articleTitle: Fabrication and characterization of Ti/TiN- based resistance temperature detector
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this work, a micro-patterned thin film resistor as temperature sensor has been developed. Based on the CMOS 1μ technology flow process, the resistance temperature detector is made. It consists of thin film of titanium/titanium- nitride as resistor. This choice is due to its widespread usage in microelectronics technology and its main properties, including specific resistivity, thermal stability, and temperature coefficient of resistance. In order to evaluate the efficiency of the suggested work, two different structures have been designed. The elaborated devices were characterized and the outcomes were examined.

articleTitle: Optimal Altitude Range for Image Collection Drone from Agricultural Areas with Image Resolution and Power Consumption Constraints
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), also known as drones are used to collect images covering an agricultural area in order to check on the condition of the crop. While the drone is hovering at a high altitude, the spatial resolution of the images becomes lower and the distance traveled to cover the whole farm is reduced, and when the drone is hovering at a low altitude, the spatial resolution of the images becomes higher and the distance traveled will be longer. Our goal is to find the appropriate altitude range for the drone to cover a farm of known length and width with image resolution and traveled distance constraints. The proposed approach considers the drone's power consumption, image resolution, and the area of interest. The optimal altitude range is determined by analyzing the trade-off between the drone's power consumption and image resolution. This research provides a valuable tool for agricultural research to optimize the drone operations in order to maximize the crop yield.

articleTitle: Simulation of a 2-R Robot Model Based on SolidWorks Design and Matlab/Simulink Trajectory Verification
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Robotic simulation is a very important step before manufacturing. The reason comes from the advantages of the simulation. Nowadays, simulation is very powerful in calculations, lower cost, flexible in design, accurate in testing, easy to change or develop the model, provides animations for presentation, etc. Path planning and obstacle avoidance are hot areas in the robotics field. So, in this paper, a model of a 2-R manipulator planer robot is presented. The simulation is done by using both SolidWorks and Matlab programs. The validation of the model is achieved by using trajectory planning. The result shows that the model of the robot successfully tracks the required trajectory.

articleTitle: Prototype of Automated Blood Specimens System
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Clinical laboratories have rapidly evolved since the 1990s, mainly driven by technological advances that focus on automation. This advanced automation nowadays helped to reduce the human errors existence. In this research, a prototype of an automated blood specimen’s system was designed and assembled, where two robotic arms carrying the blood samples from the conveyor belts to the assigned storage locations and another one to implement the dispense process. A QR reader was added to distinguish each specimen and a microcontroller is used to automate the process. Moreover, an interface system was programmed using LABVIEW software, where the coding window is different than the operator. This automated process is expected to increase the lab efficiency as well as the speed of analysis. The system was tested, and the statistical results were included that showed an average less than 4.2% error out of sixty trails.

articleTitle: Direction of arrival tracking using adaptive robust subspace decomposition and Kalman filter
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, we consider directions of arrival estimation and tracking in a noisy and relatively adverse scenario. We thus use a robust subspace tracking method called HTFAPI that exploits a weighted least squares criterion to enhance robustness, followed by a smoothing Kalman filter to improve the estimation. Simulated experiments are then presented to show that the proposed solution enhances the performance when dealing with corrupted data in an impulsive noise environment.

articleTitle: Optimized classification system for MRIs with MOO technique and SVM
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The phase of feature extraction and dimensionality reduction in pattern recognition is the way to capture the visual content images. During this phase raw images are presented in their reduced form in order to facilitate decision making in pattern recognition in general and in classification problems in particular. In this paper we propose a Magnetic Resonance Images (MRIs) classifier based on an Optimized Kernel Principal Component Analysis (OKPCA) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) named OKPCA+SVM. The ultimate objective of the proposed study is to suggest a new optimized technique of feature extraction and dimensionality reduction named OKPCA based on the Multi-Objective Optimization (MOO) method. This work is based on the following phases; preprocessing (including data acquisition), feature selection (including feature extraction and dimensionality reduction) and finally classification. The k-fold cross validation technique was applied to generalize the suggested scheme on other independent benchmarks. Two benchmarks used in our experiments are DATASET 66 and DATASET 160. The images used in the benchmarks were collected from the ‘Harvard Medical School’ website. We have found a 90.5% as accuracy rate on Dataset-66 and 91.6% as accuracy rate on Dataset-160. From the experiment results we can say that the proposed classifier is robust and effective compared to other recent studies.

articleTitle: Modified PSNR Metric for Watermarked-Image Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Digital images are exposed to different types of noise due to transformation, compression, or external data embedding. The assessment of these images is important to check their validity before being used in different applications. Because of its simplicity and straightforward calculations, the Peak Signal to Noise Ratio (PSNR) is used for evaluating digital images. PSNR, However, does not account for the human eye bias in preserving noise between textured and smooth areas. In this paper, a modified PSNR, named texture-based PSNR (T-PSNR), is proposed to enhance the PSNR metric for better image quality assessment. The metric is designed to be applied for watermarked image evaluation.

articleTitle: An EMS based on the FLC of a variable three-phase dump load Composed of PV/Fuel Cell/Battery Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: to perceive, monitor, and regulate the behavior of hybrid energy sources, an energy management system is required. The suggested system discuss in this paper integrates photovoltaics (PVs), fuel cells (FCs), and batteries. The primary goals in hybrid systems for renewable energy used fuel-cells and batteries are to reduce hydrogen consumption and maximize battery state of charge (SOC), to accomplish these goals, a fuzzy control strategy as an energy management strategy (EMS) is presented in this research to operate independently from the grid. During the day, this renewable hybrid power system relies on PV electricity as its primary source. In the dark or during times of shade, it uses the FC to provide support as a backup source. When the load power is high, the battery aids the FC. DC/DC and DC/AC converters are included in the system. Two converters DC/DC make up the power conditioning system: a boost-type unidirectional dc/dc converter for the PV and FC, and a boost-type bidirectional dc/dc converter for the battery. The key system parameters, such as FC current and battery state-of-charge (SOC), are controlled using the fuzzy control approach. It was constructed in MATLAB/Simulink in order to study and monitor the system to demonstrate the effectiveness of the fuzzy control technique. The results revealed that the system functions effectively as a micro-grid. The results reveal that the battery's SOC is maintained at an appropriate level for such batteries. The DC link voltage (VDC) is maintained at a safe level. Furthermore, the use of H2 fuel is 17 grams. There is a lot of room for cost-cutting improvements, which necessitates more study into system optimization and the use of diverse control systems.

articleTitle: Parameters Optimization of Convolutional Neural Network to Synthesize 12-Lead ECG from a 3-Lead
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents a metaheuristic optimization-based approach for reconstructing a 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) from a reduced set of leads using a convolutional neural network (CNN) model. The proposed method has two parts. The first part illustrates the optimization of the hyperparameters of the CNN model using the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) metaheuristic. The second part presents the optimization of the CNN model using a subset of the PTB diagnostic ECG database. The proposed deep learning model will be evaluated using the two-performance metrics, namely correlation coefficient (r), and root mean square error (RMSE). The results will be detailed and compared with traditional linear regression and LSTM deep learning model.

articleTitle: Determining the SoH of Lithium-Ion Batteries based on the Differential Impedance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Impedance spectroscopy is suitable for online battery diagnostics and state-of-health (SoH) estimation. Conventionally, impedance spectroscopy analysis is realized by modeling the impedance spectrum measurement with equivalent circuits. However, finding an appropriate global model can be time-consuming and challenging due to the overlap of the phenomena during the investigation. This paper proposes a novel approach for the SoH assessment based on the differential impedance analysis (DIA). The DIA extracts the charge transfer resistance and the double-layer capacitance from the impedance spectrum without relying on a global model. Furthermore, the time constant formed by the charge transfer resistance and double-layer capacitance is demonstrated to have the highest correlation for assessing the SoH of a battery. For the validation, a commercial lithium-ion battery cell of type Sony US18650VT3 is used and cycled 400 times. The results show a systematic correlation between the model parameters and the number of cycles, which forms the basis of a novel online method of SoH assessment. Moreover, the most suitable parameter to determine the SoH is the time constant τ at a frequency of 56 Hz with a coefficient of determination equal to 0.875.

articleTitle: A Microcontroller-based System for Lighting Control in an Office Building using IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Lighting is indispensable in buildings but accounts for a significant portion of energy consumption. Instead of using artificial lights that consume electricity, daylighting can significantly reduce energy consumption while pairing it with shading devices such as Venetian blinds to satisfy the visual comfort of building occupants. Indeed, artificial lighting will be used only when necessary, such as during nights and cloudy days. For these reasons, this research study proposes a design and development of a Smart Wearable System (SWS) with the Internet of Things (IoT) applications, a low-cost and low-power system on a chip microcontroller with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, that can be applied to any building to take full advantage of sunlight and improve building energy efficiency. The development of this SWS system has for objective to make it accessible and available for use in any office building in which its window(s) façade is oriented to the course of the Sun during the day. The function of this developed SWS system is to automatically adjust both the position and the slat angle of Venetian blinds according to the current Sun's position and weather situation and turns on the artificial lighting only when needed. This study ends, for now, with the presentation of simulation results obtained for the developed computer program that gives the Sun's coordinates such as azimuth and altitude for any time and day of the year.

articleTitle: New robust stability analysis for switched neutral systems with state time-delays
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The presented paper investigates the problem of robust stability for switched linear neutral time-delay systems. Indeed, the main purpose is to provide new stability conditions with the presence of disturbances and faults in the systems involved. Thus, based on Multiple Quadratic Lyapunov-Krasovskii Functions (MQLFs) methods, the novel criteria, guaranteeing robust asymptotic stability, are obtained by solving a set linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Lastly, a numerical example is given to demonstrate the pertinence of the proposed theorems.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Control For Lower Limb Rehabilitation Exoskeleton Contacting With Floor
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this study, a lower limb rehabilitation exoskeleton (LLRE) contacting with floor with uncertainties and parameter variations has been controlled using a sliding mode controller (SMC). The dynamic equations for the lower limb rehabilitation exoskeleton in case of contacting with floor in reduced order form have been derived using augmented Lagrange equations which include Lagrange multiplier and corresponding Jacobian vectors. A comparative study has been achieved between two controllers: sliding mode controller and computed torque controller. Simulation results indicate the superiority of SMC controllers over the CTC in terms of tracking error and robustness toward the uncertainties and external disturbances.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-based Climb of an Ecological Montgolfier for Large Agricultural Lands’ Supervision
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: To inspect the large agricultural lands, we propose an autonomous hot-air balloon with an ecological design, able to circumvent the large cultivation areas, in particular the olive trees in the region of Sfax which present a burden for the farmers to control them constantly. Habitually, growers and cultivators use cars and trucks either to examine trees and harvest, or to follow thieves. This inspection conduct seems to be slow, vague and energy-intensive in fuel to become a serious source of pollution. Moreover, it gives a limited view between trees. From these troublesome worries, and the pressing need of a rapid and performant solution, an ecological drone based on a hot-air balloon and photovoltaic panels is developed to resolve the major problem of large agriculture grounds. Therefore, this paper is dedicated to establishment of an autonomous Montgolfier with a detailed description of its different features. Thermodynamic and aerodynamic laws are developed to a mathematical model used in the control process. To analyze the system performances, an open-loop numerical simulation is initially carried out with an on/off relay control applied to the heater temperature. Then, a feedback control is drawn with a PID to reach a desired altitude. Finally, the PID is replaced by a Sugeno-like fuzzy controller to enhance the balloon performances in a climb phase. The paper is ended with a conclusion and next work.

articleTitle: Guardian map approach for PID and state feedback controllers synthesis
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The guardian map approach is a powerful tool for the generalized stability assessment. This tool studies the problem of parametrized matrix eigenvalues or polynomial roots confinement to a prescribed domain in the complex plane.This theory is so mature in the analysis problem, but not well used for the control synthesis purpose because the inherited complexity of the solution especially when the number of uncertain parameters is important. This paper addresses the control synthesis problem and shows how it is possible to design a PID controller for a system described by its transfer function and a state feedback controller for a state space described system. Both controllers satisfy certain performance constraints. The main idea is to consider the gains of the PID controller or the state feedback matrix entries as the parameters of a parametrized matrix family and apply the guardian map technique to find the set in which these parameters should be confined so that the desired performances can be achieved.

articleTitle: Energy Management Control of Electrical Vehicle PV Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The production and use of electric vehicles (EVs) pose new challenges, especially with the increase in energy demand. Indeed, these types of vehicles require electrical energy to charge the battery which represents the important part. In this case it is necessary to develop charging stations based on renewable energies such as photovoltaic (PV) to minimize the consumption of electrical energy based on fossil sources. In this paper, a control strategy based on fuzzy logic system is developed to control an EV charging station. This station consists of a photovoltaic energy as a primary source and an energy storage system as a secondary source. The control strategy allows to provide the power to each EV taking into account the state of charge (SoC) of the electric vehicle battery, the climatic conditions and the Soc of the storage systems. This management algorithm is tested by simulating a charging station under different conditions using the MATLAB Simulink environment. The simulation results show the efficiency of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Efficient Recursive Total Least Mean Fourth Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this work, an iterative total least mean fourth (TLMF) algorithm is devised to solve adaptive filtering problems when both the input and output signals are corrupted with noise. The proposed algorithm is based on a stochastic approach related to the existing total least mean square (TLMS) algorithm. The cost function of the TLMF is defined in terms of the fourth power of the error and minimized iteratively to reach the optimal weight solution. The unknown system is evaluated at various levels of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). The simulation results showed that the proposed algorithm produced interesting results when both the noise is white or coloured.

articleTitle: Left Ventricle Wall Motion Abnormalities Detection in Cardiac MRI
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are the main cause of death in the world. The diagnosis of these pathologies is based on physiological signals and various imaging modalities such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), ultrasound imaging and multi-arrays CT scanner. Among all these cardiac imaging modalities, MRI is a powerful tool that allows an accurate measurement of both global and regional myocardial contraction. The aim of this work is to propose an automatic method based on the combination of LSTM-U-Net architecture and the monogenic signal for detecting the dyskinesia and hypokinesia abnormalities. To detect wall motion abnormalities, a characterization and a localization of the left and right ventricles based on U-Net is first established. Once the left ventricle is detected, the monogenic signal is used to detect the direction of the endocardial contraction. The proposed algorithm was retrospectively tested on a population of 52 subjects, including 20 subjects with normal ventricular function and 32 pathological cases with hypokinesia and dyskinesia abnormalities. The results illustrate that the phase orientation is the most important parameters characterizing the left ventricle. Compared to the gold standard expert interpretation and LGE analysis, the results show that the accuracy of the proposed algorithm in the detection of hypokinesia and dyskinesia was respectively 77.27% and 82.95% while the sensitivity was 82.78% and 87.39 %. In addition, a higher specificity of 71.51% and 75.38 %,was achieved. The findings of this study illustrate the accuracy of the proposed algorithm in the detection of left ventricular wall motion abnormalities.

articleTitle: Selection of Robust Regional Computed Tomography (CT) Radiomics Features for COVID-19 for AI Based Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The lung CT images of COVID-19 patients can be characterized by three different regions – Ground Glass Opacity (GGO), consolidation and pleural effusion. Quantitative characterization of these regions using radiomics can facilitate accurate diagnosis, disease progression and response to treatment. However, according to the knowledge of the author, regional CT radiomics analysis of COVID-19 patients has not been carried out. This study aims to address these by extracting and selecting the radiomics features that can characterize each of the regions separately and can distinguish the regions from each other. Two approaches were implemented to select the features that can differentiate between lung regions – 1) one way ANOVA for finding statistical significance difference (p<0.05) between the regions and 2) Z-score and correlation heatmaps. Radiomics features that show agreement for all cases (statistical significance test, Z-score and correlation) were selected as suitable features. The features were then tested on separate 52 CT images containing GGO and consolidation. 10 radiomics features were found to be the most suitable among 44 features These features in turn can help for more accurate diagnosis, staging the severity of the disease and allow the clinician to plan for more successful personalized treatment for patients.

articleTitle: Micro-grid Power System Monitoring Design
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, a proposal is made for the design, implementation, management, and monitoring of an electrical power system that includes a main grid, a microgrid (based on a variety of forms of renewable energy and energy storage), a set of circuit breakers, and various loads. The selector switch on the control panel gives you the option of running the microgrid alone or in parallel with the central grid, and you may choose between manual, automated, and computer operation. Detailed comprehensive instructions for both software and hardware are provided.

articleTitle: Design of a 5-Gauss line system to warn persons with medical implants from critical EM field
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In some medical magnetic resonant imaging environment with a high magnetic field, there is no protection system that detects the 5-Gauss line. This region presents a serious risk zone for both the patient and the implanted device. Frequently, patients having an active medical implant like a pacemaker can cross these areas without taking into consideration that there is a harmful magnetic field. Consequently, health complications may occur. In order to overcome these issues and prevent people with pacemakers from crossing this space, we have proposed a 5-Gauss magnetic field measuring device. It detects and measures the value of the magnetic field present accompanied by an audible signal of the critical line. In our case it is equal to or greater than 5-Gauss (0.5mT). The system measures the magnetic field detected by the Hall effect SS495A sensor that is controlled by an Arduino Uno card. We performed a validation of the 5-Gauss line detection system in the medical magnetic resonant imaging environment of the military hospital of Tunis. The obtained results are very satisfactory, since the system ensures the required function.

articleTitle: Enhanced CNN Security based on Adversarial FGSM Attack Learning: Medical Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have grown in popularity for clinical image processing applications like as Covid and cancer detection. A new study, however, shows that hostile attacks with modest, unnoticeable disruptions can damage deep healthcare learning systems. This creates safety issues about using these technologies in healthcare situations. In this study, we will look at the approaches used to fight adversarial attacks on medical imaging. Next, we intend to investigate the resilience of pre-trained CNN architectures, as well as LeNet5 and MobileNetV1 models against Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) attacks in a medical healthcare application-based chest X-ray dataset. We discover that pre-trained CNN models are much more sensitive to antagonistic assaults than other models, due to key feature discrepancies between them and regular models. Finally, we propose to improve the CNN’ models security by investigating adversarial training. According to the numerical results, models with lower computational complexity and restricted layers are much more safe against malicious attacks than bigger models which are commonly utilized in medical healthcare systems.

articleTitle: Automatic diagnosis of Plant Leaf Diseases based on Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Plant disease is one of the main factors reducing crop productivity and causing massive economic loss. Therefore, early plant disease detection has a significant impact on crop quality and yield. Recently, research on the detection of crop diseases has received the utmost attention with the advancement of computer vision and deep learning technologies. In this paper, we propose an artificial intelligence-based smart agricultural system for the identification of plant diseases in Tunisia. The system is designed to detect plant leaf diseases using transfer learning-based CNN architecture. The model is trained using a dataset of 560 images collected in Tunisia with the help of an agricultural engineer. Experiment results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach for leaf disease detection.

articleTitle: Student Attendance System using iTag’s Beacon Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Tracking students’ attendance is an essential part of the educational process. The attendance is frequently done by using manual methods such as calling student names or passing around an attendance sheet. These methods are ineffective for large number of students since it requires a significant amounts of lecture time and effort, which may disturb the class. In this paper, we propose a Bluetooth-based automatic attendance management system that uses iTag. Each iTag broadcasts a beacon every specific period. The proposed system allows an automatic capturing of the surrounded beacon in a class and updates the attendance database. The user-friendly, front-end web interface of the proposed system assists the instructor to effectively manage the lecture time. Thus, the system is simple, inexpensive, and minimizes both student and instructor involvement.The key advantage of this model is to help the faculty members to give their maximum percentage of lecture time to the students. Therefore, attendance logging process can be achieved quickly and accurately.

articleTitle: Robust Calibration of Magnetometer with Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Magnetometers have a wide range of applications in inertial navigation. The calibration of the magnetometer is an essential step in magnetic field-based localization and attitude estimation. This paper is the first to present an ADMM-based algorithm for calibrating three-axis magnetometers in the presence of outliers and spurious measurements. Two pre-processing methods for outliers, truncation, and compression, are proposed. We compare the ADMM-based magnetometer calibration algorithm with other state-of-the-art methods and demonstrate the robustness and accuracy of the ADMM-based magnetometer calibration algorithm with synthetic data.

articleTitle: Cooperative PSO Heuristic for System Identification Beyond MSE Boundary in Ad-Hoc Network
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Cooperative topology of Participle Swarm Optimization (PSO) heuristic (CPSO) is implemented for system identification over ad-hoc Networks. The main achievement is the development of PSO heuristic for system identification instead of the conventional diffusion topology of the Least Mean Square called DLMS algorithm which reveals a significant improvement in terms of the Mean Square Error (MSE). The CPSO heuristic demonstrates an important MSE convergence result beyond the theoretical boundary of noise variance. In the aggregation stage, each sensor exchanges the local best objective function along with the related local best estimate to near-by neighboring sensors. The simulations indicate that the developed CPSO approach achieves extraordinary MSE and MSD improvements against existing DLMS algorithms when the input block size and population are increased.

articleTitle: Separation of multi-speaker speech from an underdetermined mixture of sources
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method of separation of multi-speaker speech from an underdetermined mixture of sources, where the number of sensors is lower than the number of speakers. For this we applied a convolution fast independent component analysis in order to determine the contributions of sources followed by a spectral subtraction technique. As post-processing, a conv-tasnet is used based a deep encoder / decoder.

articleTitle: Optimal Tracking Control for 3D Overhead Crane with Varying Time Delay and Windy Disturbance
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This study investigates the problem of tracking control for a nonlinear three-dimensional (3D) overhead crane with a changing rope, continuous windy noise, and varying time delay. The objective is to minimize the defined reward function while forcing the system output to respond to incoming signals. To create a design issue for selecting control u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(k)</inf> such that the error value is zero, thereby accomplishing tracking, establish a linear quadratic version of the performance measure that is unaffected by variable communication constraints. A technique based on an adaptive Kalman filter to gather data and then use it to design an optimal tracking controller. In addition, a simulation example is provided to illustrate the study results.

articleTitle: High Performance dual control feed forward based fuzzy logic technique & finite set control model predictive control for a grid-connected PV system
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The converters interfacing PV system with the grid involves some major drawbacks appear in simulation studies such as: An important overshoot in the steady state, the long response time, a bad power and a bad THD that exceeds IEEE standards (> 5%). That’s why in this paper two novel approaches have been proposed in order to overcome these drawbacks. As a first step, a bad tracking of the DC-link regulator is particularly apparent when the solar irradiance varies severely or suddenly, this problem leads us to develop the extension of the DC-link control using the Feed Forward based Fuzzy Logic (FF-FL) to improve transient performance of the DC-link. More developed in term of minimization error, the fuzzy is used to compensate the DC-link losses with remarkable improved performances are noted by setting DC-link voltage reference. Where in the DC link voltage Feed Forward was adapted by adjusting reference DC link voltage according to CPI (common point of interconnection). The grid side converter enables to control the active and reactive power flow to the grid and improving the output power quality by reducing total harmonic distortion (THD). The other task is dedicated to control the connection to the grid using the three-level converter in order to achieve high voltage using low voltage switching devices. In this case, Neutral Point Clamped (NPC) has been proposed to provide high output power to feed the PV source into an existing three-phase power grid via an RL filter. So, the second proposed approach deals principally with the behavior of the grid currents variation, Finite Set Control Model Predictive Control (FCS-MPC) has been proposed to exhibit the high dynamic efficiency for multilevel converters that keeps a unitary power factor injection to the grid and maximizes the energy harvested from solar. A comparison has been made between the PI and FF-FL controllers to prove the performance and the efficacy of the proposed strategy using detailed simulation studies.

Author Keywords: Grid connected converters and Finite Set Model Predictive Current Control

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of PV Power Prediction with ML Models for Improved Grid Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The need of accurate prediction models for forecasting Renewable Energies (REs) production are increasing, especially for Photovoltaic (PV) power. In this paper, we implemented and tested two models for predicting PV power, known for their good performance in wind power and load forecasting. Our results proved that these two models have much higher performance than the empirical formula and the typical Machine Learning (ML) models such as Deep Neural Network (DNN), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XG-Boost) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). The first model is based on a combination of a CNN model and a Light Gradient-Boosting Machine (LightGBM) model, which decreased the Mean Squared Error (MSE), compared to a CNN model, by 7%. In the second model, we used the Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) technique to decompose the PV power into components before training, and used LSTM and XGBoost for predicting each of the components. The second model decreased further the MSE by 45% (80% overall decrease compared to the empirical formula).<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>

articleTitle: Zonotopic Fault Estimation for Linear Parameter Varying Systems : application to wind turbine
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: A fault estimation method for a class of discrete-time Linear Parameter Varying (LPV) systems with actuator faults and measurement noise is proposed in this paper. First, an augmented descriptor approach is proposed to simultaneously estimate system states and system faults. The proposed observer is designed using L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance to minimize the uncertainties effects and to improve the estimation accuracy. Then, the envelopes of the fault can be calculated based on the obtained state estimation. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is illustrated by a case study on a 4.8MW wind turbine benchmark system.

articleTitle: Optimization-based design of fractional PID controllers for MISO systems
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of MISO systems control is studied. Two new methods are developed to design fractional PID controllers. The first one is based on the use of time-domain specifications (percentage of overshoot and setting time). It consists of minimizing a time-domain criterion without constraints. The second method is based on the use of frequency-domain specifications (phase margin φ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> and unity-gain crossover frequency ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf>). It consists of minimizing a frequency-domain criterion with respect to constraints. In both methods, a nonlinear optimization technique is used to tune the parameters of all SISO fractional PID controllers designed for all SISO subsystems composing the MISO system. The performances of fractional PID controllers are analyzed through a numerical example. They are compared to the performances obtained by the rational PI controllers.

articleTitle: Statistical analysis of Multiple Transform Selection in VVC test model (VTM)
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The promising coding efficiency enhancement of the Versatile Video Coding (VVC) over the High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) comes with a sharp increase in the encoder complexity. The additional complexity implies a real constraint related to its industrial implementation. Recently, several acceleration methods for VVC have been proposed. Yet, a deeper understanding of the VVC complexity, mainly related to the new encoding tools, is helpful to design efficient new acceleration methods. To this end, statistical analysis were conducted, focusing on the Multiple Transform Selection concept.

articleTitle: Insertion of the WindPACT turbine based on a HESG in a medium voltage network
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this study, we focused on the integration of a Hybrid Excited Synchronous Generator (HESG) based wind conversion system WCS to the grid. We presented an integrated Matlab Simulink platform to model the grid, convertors, filters, wind turbine and the generator associated to its power convertors necessary for its command. After that, we presented the detailed control strategy od the DC link as well as the grid side converter. The simulation platform is than used to test the effectiveness of the implemented control strategies in normal operation mode and in failure mode.

articleTitle: Lateral and Longitudinal Tire Force Prediction Using Soft Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: While first-principles models derived from physics laws can often approximate the system behavior, it remains difficult sometimes to capture non-physically derived behavior. The empirical formula designed by Pacejka, is among the different models of the literature that are presented to describe the tire behavior for roads with surface roughness, This formula has no physical basis and its mathematical expression is obtained from intuition and experience, but it fits well the reality of the tires. The difficulty of estimating the longitudinal and lateral forces for a broad range of tires can be solved using artificial intelligence. In this paper, both the longitudinal force as a function of longitudinal slip, s, and the lateral force as a function of the lateral slip α. Both forces are estimated using tools from artificial intelligence, where fuzzy and neural network approaches are used, excluding the need to estimate them from empirical formula. To enhance the accuracy of the performance of the estimator, we present a method for optimizing membership functions using particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, resulting in a fuzzy estimator that try to synthesize the magic formula for certain models of tires. A trained neural network is the other proposal in this paper, in which techniques from machine learning is used to realize an intelligent tire systems able to estimate these forces. Simulation results are reported, compared and discussed.

articleTitle: Efficient Thoracic aortic aneurysm detection method to prevent potential Acute Aortic Dissection
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Enlargement or aneurysm of the aorta predisposes to dissection, an important cause of sudden death. Early diagnosis of thoracic aneurysm is critical to managing the condition. The larger the thoracic aortic aneurysm, or the faster it grows, the more likely it is to rupture (dissected). The risk of rupture increases when the aneurysm is larger than about twice the normal diameter of a healthy aorta blood vessel. Diagnosing a thoracic aneurysm is difficult because often there are no symptoms, and often the condition goes undiagnosed until a rupture occurs, chest radiography is considered the first diagnosis to capture thoracic aortic enlargement. We trained a deep learning model to accurately detect and localize the present of thoracic aortic enlargement. The presented work uses single stage detection model from the You Only Look Ones (YOLO) family of detectors, in this work we followed a two-stage training strategy first starting with training on multiple pathologies, that using transfer learning strategy we implement the trained weight to trained on the detection of TAD. The obtained model shows good result achieving mean average precision mAP with threshold of 0.5 0,884 as average and 0.994 for TAD detection, other metrics such as model precision, recall and F-score shows also decent result compared to related literatures ranging between 0.827–0.83, the proposed model achieves high detection accuracy making it valuable CAD for radiologists, medical practitioners Emergency departments to minimizing aortic dilatation AD diagnosis and exclude false detection.

articleTitle: Threshold impact for CNN partitioning algorithm in the Versatile Video Coding standard
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Versatile Video Coding (VVC) standard was published in July 2020 by the Joint Video Experts Team (JVET). The VVC coding scheme has been enhanced by introducing new coding technologies compared to HEVC codec scheme. The added tools improved the Rate-Distortion (RD) performance while increasing the coding complexity. The Quadtree with Nested Multi-Type Tree (QTMT) partitioning module is one of the most complex improvement. Therefore, we suggested a low complexity QTMT algorithm based on the Convolution Neural Network (CNN). The proposed method adopted bi-threshold values in order to determine the partitioning decision according to the predicted probabilities. In this paper, a study of the bi-threshold values impact on both coding efficiency and complexity reduction is presented using the VVC reference software VTM3.0 in order to develop a method that may automatically select the appropriate bi-threshold value.

articleTitle: Transmission Tower Detection and Camera Re-centering Embedded system based on Image processing
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Overhead power line monitoring in real-time is a hot subject since such a process offers the possibility of charging the overhead power line with higher currents. Existing systems for overhead power line monitoring often provide inaccurate data or possess the disadvantage that they have to be mounted directly at the conductor. Installation of such systems is only possible with the building of a new overhead line or goes hand in hand with cutting off the voltage. Therefore, installation on existing overhead lines and the maintenance of the systems lead to high costs. As a solution, in our previously conducted work, we proposed a monitoring system for overhead power lines. This system is equipped with a camera, which was installed on one tower and aimed at the opposite one. Using modern image processing methods, the sag was detected. The system is mounted on the power pole and not on the conductor. As a result, installation and maintenance can be done at a low cost. Although we were able to achieve high accuracy because the sag is measured directly without the use of auxiliary variables, we still needed to ensure that the camera is centered prior to the sag calculation process. This paper presents a method for tower detection and automatic camera repositioning to maintain the desired symmetry. This led to higher accuracy and brought us one step closer to a fully autonomous system, which means less need for human intervention and, moreover, lower labor costs.

articleTitle: Bagging and Voting Deep Learning Ensemble Methods for Binary Classifications of Solar Panel Cells Defects
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Rain, extreme heat, and humidity are typical unpleasant weather conditions that solar panels are exposed to. This has an impact on photovoltaic panel cells and hence leads to various defects. Therefore, it takes time to manually inspect these defects, especially in large solar panel plants. In this study, we propose to implement the voting and bagging deep learning ensemble models' techniques to the images of photovoltaic panel cells, which are captured by drones with electroluminescence cameras, to diagnose faulty cells. To efficiently identify and classify defects, a benchmark of solar photovoltaic images that are compiled based on the electroluminescence phenomena is used. This dataset is combined to form a binary classification. One class is functional cells, and the other is defective cells. Then, an experiment of five deep learning vision models, using SENet, Vision Transformer (Vit), Xception, GoogleNet, and ResNet18, are applied as estimators to the bagging and voting ensemble techniques. Based on the results, both ensemble methods have the highest accuracy of 72.804% for voting and 72.222% for bagging as compared with 61.15% of the hybrid of ResNet50 and Inception V3 models.

articleTitle: Online PV panel characterisation for PV system diagnostic
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Photovoltaic PV systems are widely installed to produce green electrical energy in recent years due to its high reliability, installation simplicity, and zero fuel costs. Many research works prove that PV cells and modules are influenced by climatic conditions perturbations. In this way, many diagnosis methods have been developed, among them that based on the PV current and voltage analysis. In this paper, an online PV system I-V characterization using two-diode model has been investigated to study the health of an operating PV system. An iterative algorithm to extract the online real I-V characteristic is explored in this paper. The proposed method is validated on an experimental setup composed of a PV panel, a DC/DC converter and a resistive load. The DC/DC duty cycle ratio variation allows to extract experimental I-V curve portion for 60%V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf> ≤ V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">PV</inf> ≤ V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf>. The implemented algorithm allows the estimation of the short circuit current for a given irradiance and temperature through the adjustment of internal parameters, if needed, of the PV two-diode model. The obtained results are used to study the health state of the PV system.

articleTitle: FDI based extended kalman filter for multi robot system
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper the problem of detection and isolation (FDI) in wheeled mobile robot is treated. first of all we consider a master-slave robot system in which the master robot has to follow a desired trajectory given by a well-determined control law, then the slave is controlled by the master. However in real environment there is no ideality because faults can appear in the master or slave or even the both and affect the system and may lead to unacceptable results so to ensure a well functioning an extended kalman filter is tuned to diagnosis eventual faults and to generate residuals in order to detect and isolate them. The performance of an estimator based on an EKF is simulated based MATLAB Simulink simulations.

articleTitle: Effects of electrical energy storage devices on frequency management in various typical power system operating situations
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In linked electric power systems with various generating units, energy storage is crucial for maintaining frequency regulation. If load frequency control (LFC) capability is unable to balance out generation and demand mismatches, enormous frequency variations will manifest. One of the greatest solutions to handle these problems and keep the balance between energy generation and demand is quick-acting energy storage systems. The primary goal of this study is to examine how quickly responsive energy storage devices can be used to control frequency in contemporary power systems with various generating units. With regard to several typical power system operating scenarios, the effects of electrical energy storage systems such as superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) and capacitive energy storage (CES) have been examined. These storage solutions exhibit encouraging outcomes in the power systems under investigation.

articleTitle: Design of Super twisting MPPT Controller Using DC-DC ZETA converter
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Solar energy is ecologically beneficial and has an infinite supply in nature.
