To obtain electricity from the sun photovoltaic panels are required, which convert solar energy into electricity. hand the difficulty of gathering power from a solar system while minimizing power losing is involved with the PV array power providing capabilities and the kind of the output. Different climatic circumstances and the complex performance of PV systems make tracking fluctuating maximum power points difficult. Changing climatic status and the nonlinear action of PV systems make tracking fluctuating maximum power points difficult Given the nonlinearity of a Pv module, in a PV system, a (Maximum power point) algorithm is required to direct the operation at (MP) and thus maximize the power generated. in this research document we proposed a MPPT controller to extract the maximum power point from fo PV module connected to ZETA converter.the seggested control compare with P&O algorithm in stady state and variation in irradiation using MATLAB/SIMULINK toolbox as a result the proposed STWC for ZETA converter give batter perferman and less fluctuation around the maximum power point (MPPT).

articleTitle: Design and concept of a low-pass filter for the UHF band
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, we simulate and design a "low-pass filter for UHF band applications". The developed structures have good agreement between simulated and experimental results, with an estimated error of a 4,848 %. The simulated structure has a cut-off frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>= 1.877 GHz and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>=1.786 GHz obtained from the design result.

articleTitle: FEA based Investigation of Discoid Rotor Sizing Effect on the ClaW Pole TFPM Performances
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The claw pole transverse flux permanent magnet synchronous machine (TFPM) with discoid rotor present a new configuration of TFPM with a stator which contains teeth allowing the conduction of the flux in the axial direction from the poles of a discoid rotor into the stator. The machine is with an axial air gap, in contrast to the previous designed claw pole machines, this gives the possibility to operate with one rotor disc for two stator phases. FEA comparative study between the cylindrical and discoid rotor design for the same machine volume is presented in this work The rotor sizing is a necessity for the study of the machine performance and cost, the effect of the discoid rotor depth on the torque production is studied to improve the performance, the effect of this parameter on the two phase machine is studied in this case for a machine with two separated rotor. For the study of the effect of the rotor depth on the machine vibration, the FEA of the cogging torque is carried in this work.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Fuzzy Logic Control and PI Control for DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper aims at improving the performance of a DC Microgrid System, by introducing different control strategies and testing the performance of each. The components of this system are PV-source, power converters, and storage systems. The overall system will first be designed to be able to test the improvement of using the control strategies. Simulink will be used to implement the system modeling and testing. Different control schemes could be used in this context, such as fuzzy logic controller.

articleTitle: Modeling and Characterization of a Hydroelectric Transducer for Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: One of the most innovative solutions to both limit battery consumption and increase the use of renewable energy is based on the use of autonomous energy systems. This challenge is accomplished through energy harvesting devices in order to convert any form of energy into electricity. The specific conversion is usually application driven, in fact the specific application usually presents the actual form of energy that can be harvested and converted to power up the system. In particular in this paper a water flow measurement system is considered and one of the feasible applications is to utilize a system consisting of a transducer to convert the kinetic energy of a water flow into electrical energy. In this manner the measure itself is the one quantity providing the energy the measurement system that therefore includes and exploits an energy harvesting device. For this study, a voltage generator readapted as a transducer made of a three-phase motor and a rectifier circuit is used. The aim of this paper is the presentation of the models representing the features of the transducer, the experimental set-up used for the characterization and the analysis of the measurements accomplished in order to demonstrate the suitability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Determining the Dynamic Parameters of a Robot Using the Method of Instrument Variables
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The identification of robot dynamic parameters is usually based on the use of the reverse model which is linear in relation to the dynamic parameters to be identified. In order to get an overdetermined system, this model is sampled while the robot is trained with fascinating movements. The optimum solution is obtained with linear least squares (LCL). The efficacy of this approach has been demonstrated through the experimental identification of numerous industrial prototypes and robots. It has been expanded to other systems including compactors, cars, engines and haptic interfaces. Though, this method requires accurate measurement at a fairly high rate of torque and position image. It also requires estimating speeds and accelerations by band-pass filtering positions. This results in a noisy observation matrix. Furthermore, the identification is done in a closed loop due to the unstable nature of the robots' dual integrator. The instrumental variable (IV) method addresses the problem of the noisy observational matrix and can be statistically optimal. This article highlights this technique and proposes an extension of this method which is applied to a flat robot of 2 degrees of freedom (DOF).

articleTitle: CapDC: A new capuchin search based algorithm for efficient data collection in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Despite the widespread applications of Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) in different domains, several challenges such as energy, throughput and load balancing that substantially impact the network’s lifetime exist. Devising efficient clustering and routing strategy is treated as a viable solution to these challenges. Previous research has proven that meta-heuristic algorithms are successful in providing an optimal or near-optimal outcome with limited computational resources in an acceptable time period. In view of this, we introduce a new capuchin search based algorithm for efficient data collection in WSNs (CapDC). CapDC is a hybrid Capuchin Search (CapSA) and Ant Colony optimization (ACO) algorithms, which is an integration of CapSA and ACO. CapSA identifies the best cluster heads while ACO accomplishes energy-efficient routing, which reduces energy usage and enhances WSN lifetime. The results reveal that the CapDC improves residual energy usage, throughput and WSN lifetime significantly.

articleTitle: Control of an Electrical System by Recurrent Neural Network RSOM map
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper discusses an intelligent strategy using the Recurrent Self Organizing Map RSOM for anomaly detection over a motor pump. The proposed idea involves the most significant features of RSOM to locate and appreciate the fault origin. It concerns the topological structure of the map, the unsupervised deep learning algorithm, as well as the Unified Modeling Language (UML) activity diagram. The measurement and treatment of the coming signal from an appropriate sensor fixed on the experimental bench, was doneat a precise moment in the Automatism and Industrial Computing Laboratory. A comparative analysis of the flaw detection performance was carried out using the RSOM neural map and the spectral analysis method.

articleTitle: A smart HMI interface for an H2/O2 Anti-COVID machine
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The excessive need for H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gases following the spread of the covid'19 pandemic are prompting the whole world cover the increased lack of these two vital gases. Hydrogen gas is a new and promising treatment option for a variety of diseases especially covid'19.An electrolyzer machine has been industrialized to improve O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> production. This electrolyzer is equipped with a human-machine interface designed to facilitate communication between the user and the machine. This interface also allows for the early detection of any faults in the sensors installed on this electrolyzer.Touchscreen operator panels proved to be a suitable replacement for classical operator panels for implementing human-machine interfaces (HMIs). This paper introduces a new technique for HMIs design in electrolyzer to control different parameters such us temperature, pressure, and flow. It provides a new method to detect machine failure by using Deep Learning.

articleTitle: Solving Inverse Kinematics for 3R Manipulator Using Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Manipulator robots are one of the widely famous robotics types. One of the major problems that appear when preparing these robots is the Inverse Kinematic Problem (IKP). Overcoming the IKP in some cases requires solving complex equations, time-consuming, and can lead to singularity solutions. In this paper, a modeling of the forward kinematics for a 3-R manipulator robot was carried out to generate a dataset for supervised learning. Furthermore, a training model for solving the inverse kinematics of this robot with avoiding the singularity points based on Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) is proposed. The reliability of the method was validated by trajectory tracking. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the robot to track the referenced path successfully with maximum mean absolute error in the X, Y, and Z axes around 1.375 mm.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis between SQP and PSO approaches with components tolerances effect for optimizing a one MW PV substation
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The main objective of this study is to focus on the impact of the tolerances of power components (mainly inductors and capacitors) on the design of a one MW PV substation. This is highlighted through a comparative analysis of two optimization algorithms: (i) A deterministic optimization based on the Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) approach [1], and (ii) A meta-heuristic optimization based on the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) approach [2], [3].In this work, an improvement to the Selective Harmonic Elimination (SHE) [4], [5] control strategy is suggested to provide higher grid-generated energy quality and make the design of a real case of a one MW PV substation less sensitive to component tolerances.

articleTitle: Optimization of Microfluidic-Integrated Sensor for COVID-19 Application
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: COVID-19 is a pandemic disease caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). This virus is mainly spread by droplets, respiratory secretions, and direct contact. Caused by the huge spread of the COVID-19 epidemic, research is focused on the study of biosensors as they present a rapid solution for reducing incidents and fatality rates. In this paper, the fluid flow inside the microchannel has been analyzed in order to optimize the biosensor time detection. A numerical simulation based on two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations has been used. The study has been carried out for different inlet positions and several confinement velocities. In addition, the effect of inlet angles on time detection has been analyzed. Results revealed that biosensor time detection is enhanced with a closer secondary inlet position and higher velocity confinement. Further, the inlet angle has a slight effect on time detection.

articleTitle: 3D Geometry Design of the Human Thorax and Forward Calculation for Electrical Impedance Tomography
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) for lung monitoring reflects the internal conductivity distribution of human tissues based on the boundary voltages that are measured through given electrodes. The electrodes are placed around the human chest. A low-amplitude current is injected through driving electrodes, and the boundary voltages are measured through other electrodes. In this context, this work has elaborated a strategy for the design of a 3D geometry of the human thorax based on sequential Computed Tomography (CT) scans. This geometry will be used for the simulation and analysis of the EIT measurement. Image segmentation has been used to extract the contour within different layers of the CT scans to form the final 3D geometry of the chest containing the lungs and the thorax. The generated geometry was later meshed and repaired. Mesh properties were controlled through the Skewness quality metric. A multi-layered design has been elaborated to mimic different human chest layers such as body fluid, muscle, and skin resulting in three models. These models had given the accuracy of 62%, 63%, and 65% of skewed elements relative to the existing volume. Later on, the electrodes were placed on the thorax geometry for EIT forward simulation, and the effect of the multi-layered model has been investigated.

articleTitle: On The Effect Of Optical Power On Quantum Dot HEMT Transistor
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: We have investigated the DC Characteristics of AlGaAs/GaAS High electron Mobility Transistor in which a layer of InAs self-assembled Quantum Dots was inserted below the Two-Dimensional Electron Gas (2DEG) channel. A plateau and hysteresis loops appeared in the current-voltage characteristics at low Temperatures in dark and illumination conditions which led to an increase of Negative Differential Conductance with the rise of optical power. Electrical Measurements showed that the plateau and hysteresis disappeared at a Critical Temperature value of 150 K. Optical memory effect was demonstrated for the studied sample which could be useful for low-Temperature Electronics (e.g Space Application).

articleTitle: Adaptive Higher order finite-time sliding mode control for master-slave manipulator with fixed-time delays
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive second order nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode control is proposed for the tracking problem of a teleoperation system. A robust control law is developed to achieve high precision tracking and strong robustness against parametric uncertainties, external disturbances, and time-varying delay. Meanwhile, through involving the discontinuous function into the time derivative of the control input, the proposed control scheme eliminates the chattering phenomenon and reduces the amplitude of the control effort. Furthermore, an adaptive tuning law is derived to avoid the prior knowledge of the upper bound of the compound disturbances, which is more efficient for practical applications. The stability of the system is proved using the Lyapunov theory.

articleTitle: 5G Wireless Communications Performance Enhancement-Based VANET technology
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing is considered as a powerful technique that supports the needed recent technologies data rates. Thus, in this work it has been proposed to enhance the vehicular communications as a candidate in the 6G communication systems. The QoS for such systems is a crucial factor; therefore, this work tackles the QoS from both of the power consumption point of view and of the latency enhancements.In this paper, the QoS modification has been made based on two stages; the reduction of the base stations latency and introducing the multiparalell processing stage. Accordingly, antenna deployment process has been proposed in addition to make use of Daubechies wavelet to overcome the peak to average power ratio problem. The efficiency of the proposed work will be compared to both of the literature work and our previously published work.An extensive simulation has been done, which shows he effectiveness of the proposed work. It outperforms the state-of the artwork and gives a 12% performance enhancement of our previously published work.

articleTitle: Influence of the load variations on the PSS performance during steady state and transient state
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The load on a power station varies from time to time due to uncertain demands of the consumers and is known as variable load on the station. Also it is known to have an effect on the performance of a power system stabilizer while damping inter-area oscillation. In this paper conventional lead lag PSS and PSS2B are assessed on real case studies; Peerdawod Gas power station in north of Iraq- Erbil. The PSS utilizes the local rotor speed and power as its input. To investigate the effects of dynamic loads on power systems stability, the effectiveness of PSS is tested and compared with the variation of loads during and after sadden faults. The simulation software that used MatlabTM/Simulink; and results of this paper contribute to the understanding of how load variations influence the system damping based on PSS.

articleTitle: Modeling and Optimisation of a Hybrid Energy Harvesting System for IoT Nodes Through PSO-MPPT
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The principal contribution of this research paper is to propose an efficient hybrid solar-wind energy harvesting approach that can be used as a solution to the limited battery energy problem of IoT nodes. Ideally, the IoT Network nodes using optimized Solar-wind Energy Harvesting should function for many years. In order to obtain the optimal power for a hybrid system, the Maximum power point tracking (MPPT) based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) controller is proposed. This is by adjusting the duty cycle of the boost converter for both Solar and wind system based on voltage and current measurements. During this work, the modeling and simulation of the proposed hybrid system with PSO−MPPT technique under various wind speeds and various irradiation levels are done using MATLAB/SIMULINK. The Battery Condition of Charge (SoC), battery voltage and battery Current are evaluated. Simulation results prove that the proposed hybrid system with MPPT using PSO can provide better performance as compared to the Perturb and Observe (P&O) method. The proposed system has the potential to meet the energy demand of IoT nodes. increases the durability, and total efficiency of the IoT devices, making them perpetually powered.

articleTitle: KUKA Robot Language Parser for Product Adaptive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The work reported in this paper enables to upload and activation of new programs to KUKA industrial robots during active operation, which would not be possible normally. By doing this it is possible to program those robots offline resulting in increased flexibility for modern manufacturing. The programs could be placed on work pieces to form a work-piece-driven production. Comparable projects increased the capabilities of robot programming by avoiding the KUKA Robot Language using high-level programming languages. Those approaches have proven themselves in the field of research. Nevertheless, this work tries a completely different approach by enabling offline programming and switching between programs while maintaining KRL the most used robot programming language for KUKA robots.

articleTitle: Closed-loop identification practice of two-shaft gas turbine variables with reliable linear control approach
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The practice of control strategies and their applications on industrial systems requires reliable models in implementation, with an identification of their variables involved in the control sequence. Indeed, several complexity limitations of these systems require the use of linearization around the operating points, to ensure the stability of the system. To this end, this work proposes the development of a closed-loop identification strategy, applied to a two-shaft gas turbine, using a linear control with state feedback. This approach makes it possible to meet stability objectives by ensuring better performance in control variables of the studied gas turbine.

articleTitle: Arbitrary-Oriented Arabic Scene Text Annotation Based DeepAL and Scale-Aware Data Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: One of the most important and widely utilized components of communication is visual text, which is widely employed in our daily interactions. Therefore, finding and using this textual information is quite important. The detection of Arabic text in scene images is a difficult and complex field of research. Scene text detection is affected by a complex background, various font sizes, and random orientations. Modern deep learning techniques have produced impressive results for both accuracy and precision values when used to detect text in natural scene images, while the images generated with these techniques cannot reproduce the complexity and variability of natural images. Wherefore, as a fast and efficient solution, we propose a deep active learning (DeepAL) detector system based on Scale-Aware Data Augmentation and Transfer Learning to reduce significantly the number of training samples required and also to minimize the annotation work for Arbitrary-Oriented Arabic scene text, we have used the Tunisia Street View Dataset (TSVD) [1].

articleTitle: Read and write circuit for memristive neural networks
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new method for programming memristor conductance in a neural network. The circuit has been designed using an enhanced generalized memristor model (EGM) incorporating both read and write operations. This circuit exploits the pulse programmability of the memristor without the need for external processing to precisely set the conductance to a given state. The performance of the circuit has been validated by simulation with the EGM model and the results show good linearity between the programmed state of the memristor and the input reference voltage.

articleTitle: A New Mutimodel approach for modelling of fractional order interval transfer functions
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper is focused on uncertain fractional order systems. In this context, a new modelling approach of uncertain fractional order systems represented by an explicit fractional order interval transfer function is proposed. This approach is based, essentially, on multimodel approach. In fact, firstly, two new determination methods of models’ library, inspired from the Kharitonov approach, are exposed. Then, we propose to compute the validity degree of each model of the obtained library, by optimizing a constrained least squares problem. The global model is, finally deduced by fusion of outputs of the different library’ models. To prove its efficiency and its precision, the proposed approach is then compared to the approximation approach of Oustaloup through two simulation examples.

articleTitle: Stabilization control for LPV neutral time delay descriptor systems
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In the present work, the synthesis of stabilization method for neutral time delay LPV models systems is considered. In first time, a state feedback control is designed, aiming to develop a stabilization control strategy that maintains stability and desired performance in a closed-loop system. In this case, the LMI (Linear Matrix Inequality) analytical method used to determine the feedback gain of the controller. In second time and in the case of malfunction a fault diagnosis study is presented in this paper based on an Adaptive Polytopic Observer (APO). The numerical example shows the effectiveness of the obtained results.

articleTitle: A Super-twisting Algorithm based the Sliding Mode Control Applied on the Speed Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine*
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper deals a super-twisting algorithm based the sliding mode control (STA-SMC) applied on the speed permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM). Achieving good characteristics performance to the speed of PMSM drive under the influence of the most difficult scenarios that occur during the drive operation as well as to overcome the problems of the previous approaches sliding mode control. STA-SMC technique has the robustness feature under the uncertainties like parameter variation of the drive, disturbances like load torque applied and the speed levels change among low, medium and high speed. Moreover, it affords remarkable improvements, including the performance stability of both the sliding surface and the state variables together, fast finite-time convergence and its switching law developer based on a novel strategy which contributes to reducing the chattering problems afflicted by previous approaches sliding mode control; in addition, it also offers optimum performance characteristics such as smaller settling time, steady state error and without overshoot initial. Furthermore it, the effectiveness of the control under the scenarios mentioned above is validated using Matlab/Simulink simulation.

articleTitle: Solar Irradiance Forecasting using Gaussian Process Regression Model
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Photovoltaic power generation presents a significant problem for power system security due to their stochastic nature. Thus, photovoltaic energy forecasting plays a key role in addressing the challenges of grid stability. Then, accurate PV energy forecasting improve the output power and therefore reduce the need for reserve energy to balance energy. Also, it improves dispatch and planning power. In this paper, we study a short term forecasting of PV power using a Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) model. The meteorological conditions such as temperature is used as input, while solar irradiance, is used as output for GPR model.The data set are illustrated from data NOAA'S Surface Radiation (SURFRAD) Network at Bondville station, located in the USA. A comparative study with other machine learning techniques is developed in terms of calculation time (CT), RMSE, MAE, and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> .

articleTitle: Soil-based Sensor for Measurements of Static Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper examines a novel soil-based sensor for measurements of static or quasi-static magnetic fields. The proposed sensor falls under the rubric of green, non-toxic, eco-friendly, low cost, disseminable and mimetic sensors. It is worth noting that the solution here addressed aims to overcome potential problems of "traditional" silicon-based solutions that could present issues in terms of environmental pollution or biodegradability and toxicity. In particular the working principle together with finite elements numeric simulation and experimental validation will be presented demonstrating the suitability of the proposed approach in areas of interest for security applications, measurements of variable ferromagnetic materials and changes in DC magnetic field.

articleTitle: Integration of Lightweights Blocks Ciphers as an Extension into Microprocessor for IoT Security
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The Internet of Things today is in all areas of daily life. It changes all sectors including industry, agriculture, and smart homes. Therefore, IoT devices require secure microprocessors for data security. However, these devices are limited in terms of computing power, surface, memory, and in terms of energy consumption. In this article, we will present a new customized version of LEON3, the RISCV (Reduced Instruction Set Computer-five) processor, dedicated to IoT applications with a powerfully built security mechanism integrated at the design stage. Also, we presented the proposed lightweight cryptographic algorithm instructions (LED and SIMON), which are integrated into the new architecture of the ReonV processor. After integrating the lightweight encryption instructions to ensure security, we have implemented our custom processor on FPGAs and are evaluated for slice LUT plus FF pairs and frequency. The obtained results show that our proposed designs can achieve good encryption results with high performance and low cost for our new RenoV processor architecture Compared to previous works.

articleTitle: Gravity compensation and fractional control of lower limb exoskeleton
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper we study the control of a lower limb exoskeleton dedicated for Kid’s rehabilitation. A fractional order proportional-derivative (FOPD) control with constant gravity compensation is proposed for the regulation of a robot with two joints. The control law requires the measure of the position and the used torque of the two joints. The goal is to stabilize the robot in a desired trajectory with less error and energy.A simulation study reveals the better performance that can be obtained with the fractional proportional derivative with gravity compensation as compared to an FOPD for the first performance criteria (the IAE) and the PD with gravity compensation for the second criteria (the IAU).

articleTitle: Offgrid Portable Solar PV system for Emergency Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Solar PV system in Jordan has a high potential and studies shows that solar radiation is in range (5 to 7) kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and enjoys a high potential for about 330 sunny days per year. One of the modified designs on photovoltaic systems that are not connected to the electrical grid is the off-grid mobile PV generator. It contains an integrated system capable of producing electric power up to 2kWh/day with storage batteries as a backup. These systems are compact, small and can be transferred to any location easily by being hooked to a truck or any other vehicle. PV arrays mounted on the main body are able to be closed and opened in order to save space and make it easy for the system to be transported. Also, it can be set so quickly, therefore they can be considered an extremely smart solution to many situations involved in producing electricity. For example, disaster areas such as flooding and earthquakes, dispersed population and camping place. The research work in this paper will cover the design to manufacture stage of 1kW PV mobile system, while building the prototype and testing the complete system will be the next stage of the proposed work.

articleTitle: Design of Antenna for 5G Applications at 80 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, we will present a patch antenna operating in 80 GHz frequency for 5G applications. We will perform a parametric study considering the influence of the different geometrical (dimensions) and physical (substrate…) parameters to improve the antenna at 80GHz to see the impact of these parameters on the characteristics of the designed antenna. There are several specialized electromagnetic simulators for microwave design. Among these simulators, we will use CST for our study. Good results in terms of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> (-34dB), gain (7dB), wide band in the order of 2 GHz and efficiency (60%) are achieved

articleTitle: On the Use of Undersampled Signals for Power Amplifiers Linearization Using Digital Predistortion
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper investigates the use of under-sampled feedback signals for the synthesis of digital predistortion functions. The use of under-sampled feedback signals typically requires a computationally complex signal reconstruction algorithm. In this work, it was shown that the computational complexity of such process can be significantly reduced by allowing for an imperfect reconstruction of the full-rate signal. This was found to have minimal impact on the linearization capability of the digital predistorter. Experimental validation on a commercial GaN based power amplifier was carried out using a 5G new radio having a bandwidth of 20MHz. The results show that up to 80% reduction in the computational complexity of the signal reconstruction algorithm can be achieved by allowing for a 1dB tolerance in the normalized mean squared error, which in turns results in a few dB degradation in the adjacent channel leakage ratio measured at the output of the linearized amplifier.

articleTitle: ECG Data Forecasting Based on Linear Models Approach: a Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper investigates the replacement of the surface electrodes (physical sensors) measuring the electrocardiogram (ECG) signals by forecasting linear algorithms. The aim is to test the ability to overcome the loss of information in case of failure of any electrode. From real ECG signals measured in different auscultation sites, the ability to predict the ECG signal of one site depending on another site is evaluated by 3 methods. In this paper, based on quantitative criteria, a comparative study between Linear regression (LR) model, K-nearest neighbors model (KNN) and Random forest regression (RFR). The advantages and drawbacks of each one are also highlighted also that the three models are very accurate in building a new ECG signal.segment similar to the real signal.

articleTitle: Optimal Control and Balancing of Double Inverted Pendulum using Linear Quadratic and Model Predictive Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper compares two linear control methods, LQR and MPC, in the context of controlling and stabilizing the Double Inverted Pendulum, a highly unstable and nonlinear system. While the use of LQR to control this system is well-established, MPC has emerged as an alternative that has shown to be effective. The study examines the impact of incorporating Laguerre functions in the MPC approach, as it has the potential to reduce computational load while maintaining dynamic performance. The results were obtained through simulations conducted in MATLAB.

articleTitle: Comparative Study Between Classical and Fuzzy Logic DTC Strategies Aimed to an IPMSM Drives
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This Direct torque control strategy involves the estimation of stator flux and electromagnetic torque based on measured of stator currents and voltages of motor drives. Based on the errors between the reference and estimated values of mentioned variables, it’s possible to control directly the inverter states in order to reduce the control variables errors within the prefixed limits of hysteresis bands. Moreover, there is no difference in control action between big and small torque errors, due to the nature of hysteresis control adopted in classical DTC strategy. An ultimate solution is to divide the torque error into different intervals and gives different control voltages for each of them. To deal with this purpose, two fuzzy logic controllers for both motor speed and torque are proposed along with DTC strategy. So, the principle and tuning procedure of the fuzzy logic DTC scheme are investigated, to improve the system performance providing fast dynamic responses and reduced torque ripples and current distortions.

articleTitle: IoT Based Control of Robotic Manipulator using Arbotix-M Microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Robotic manipulator is one of the most important robotic devices that finds a wide variety of applications in industries. There is a lot of research done in past to control the robotic manipulator using the classical control methods. A lot of experimental work has been performed as well to control the robots using different hardware set up. With the advancement in technology, and development of smart devices, the control of robotic manipulator using Internet of Things (IoT) is one of the favorites research topics recently. The Arbotix-M microcontroller is one of the most powerful microcontrollers that can control multiple servo motors simultaneously. In literature there is very few works which uses Arbotix-M microcontroller, Therefore, in this research we design an IoT based control of a five degree of freedom robotic manipulator using Arbotix-M Microcontroller and XBee module. The experiments were performed on pincher-X 150 robot with simulation done in C++. The robot successfully performed pick and place operation controlled using remote PC.

articleTitle: Investigation on NO2 sensing behavior of WO3 nanograined resistive sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The gas sensing performance of chemoresistive metal-oxide sensors are influenced by different factors concerning both the material chemical structure and the sensor preparation. Among them, the grain size is a critical factor that plays an important role in determining the gas response of the sensor. In this work the sensing behavior of a WO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> nanograined resistive sensor at low concentrations of NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is investigated by means of experimental tests. The realized sensor shows outstanding sensing performance in the observed working temperature range between 175 °C - 265 °C for NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentrations below 10 ppm. The analysis carried out also provides important information on the influence of the nanostructure of the film in the dynamics of the response of the sensor to the gas and to the chemical reactions involving the material surface.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle driven by PMSM
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: High power density and torque inertia rotation are two advantages keys of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) which are widely used in electrical vehicles (EVs). Nowadays, research focuses on the development and the improvement of this type of vehicles due to its environmental and economic benefits such as reduction of CO2 emissions. This paper discusses some of the fundamental contributions of control strategies for PMSM applied to electric vehicles considering the conventional control method such as Field Orientation Control (FOC) and Direct Torque Control (DTC) with relevant merits and shortcomings. In this paper, the mathematical model of an IPMSM and the dynamic model of EV is presented, along with a brief description of the main types of EVs.

articleTitle: Enhanced U-Net Approach: Semantic Segmentation for Self-Driving Cars Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Semantic segmentation is a crucial task for the development of autonomous vehicles. Autonomous Driving (AD) stack is mainly classified into three subsystems, which are respectively control, planning, and perception. This work deals with the perception subsystem of AD systems. Indeed, on-road semantic segmentation for the AD systems is addressed using deep-learning algorithms. This paper proposes a deep learning approach based on an enhanced U-Net model that exploits squeeze and excitation (SE) networks. In order to demonstrate the efficiency of the added SE blocks, we opted to use U-Net as our baseline. In these experiments, the two models are trained from scratch on the CamVid dataset. Compared with the U-Net baseline, the mean class accuracy (mCA) and the mean intersection over union (mIoU) of the proposed model are increased by 5.54% and 5.87%, respectively. It achieves a mIoU of 59.88 % and a mCA of 84.15% on the CamVid dataset. The achieved results reveal that the improved U-Net reaches a better compromise between accuracy and computational complexity than previous studies.

articleTitle: Functional Interval Observers-Based Fault Detection for Multivariable Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper considers fault detection (FD) problem for multivariable Linear Parameter-Varying (LPV) systems with actuator fault and additive disturbances. An L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance is presented in order to improve the accuracy of the proposed residual framers and to attenuate the effects of the uncertainties. The sufficient conditions of the observer design are developed in terms of Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs) constraints using the Lyapunov stability theory. Eventually, the effectiveness of the proposed methodology is illustrated by a numerical example.

articleTitle: Multi-parallel Processing based OFDM for Combatting PAPR
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: AbstractOFDM is considered as a powerful technique in these days technologies since it is capable to support high data rates. This powerful technique has a major deficiency from the power management point of view. This work proposes a multiparalell algorithm based on wavelets function to tackle this issue.A MATLAB simulation has been performed to validate this work and to compare it with the Logarithmic Rooting Companding technique. From the simulated results, the average peak power has been minimized and enhanced with a ratio of 15% over the literature.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Low-IF Hartley Image-Reject Receiver for Multi-standard Wireless applications and IoT Domain
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: A dual-band Low-IF Hartley image-reject architecture for multi-standard wireless applications and IoT domain is presented. The Lower Side Band (LSB) is set to be the image band when the desired band is the Upper Side Band (USB), and vice versa. The various blocks parameters of RF receiver front end are simulated and optimized to meet receiver specifications. The receiver simulations show a cascaded gain (CGAIN) of 50 dB, a Cascaded Noise Figure (CNF) of about 1.07 dB, a 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order Input Intercept Point (IIP3) of -6 dBm, a Spurious Free Dynamic Range (SFDR) of 71 dB and an Error Vector Magnitude (EVM) less than 1%.

articleTitle: Mobile Robot Modelling and Design of Kinematic Controller for trajectory tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Forever and ever, autonomous mobile robots are an object of discussion but nowadays it’s an emerging topic due to the all progress related to field like autonomous driving. A mathematical model is very critical to begin in the mobile robotics field, that’s why this paper provides a mathematical model of unicycle mobile robot with two wheels is determined by kinematic and dynamic model. Also, a kinematic controller was designed and improved. This is the first step in research based on mobile robotics to find optimal and improved solutions for autonomous vehicles. The effectiveness of the simulated code is demonstrated by simulating a two-wheeled unicycle mobile robot using Matlab code and simulations.

articleTitle: PWM based Software defined radio Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Modern wireless networks are allocated in different frequency bands and have different specifications. However, many wireless devices are required to support different standards which is the case for mobile devices and IoT. For example, a modern mobile device usually supports 5G or 4G besides older generations back to 2G, Wi-Fi standards 802.11 a/b/g/n/ac and Bluetooth with its different versions. To support all these standards, an increasing complexity is added to the design of RF front-end that should be more flexible and more programmable.Software-defined-radio SDR aims to achieve a flexible front-end that is fully programmable and flexible in order to support more standards in different frequency bands and with different specifications. It takes advantage of the increasing enhancements in IC fabrication processes which enables performing signal processing in digital domain with high speed and accuracy more than what analog signal processing can achieve.In this work, a review of traditional receivers as well as multistandard receivers and SDRs are performed, then an SDR based on Pulse-width-modulation PWM RF-to-digital receiver is demonstrated. The chosen PWM based SDR is modeled using MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: Connected Parking for smart cities: Prototype and Android Application
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents an intelligent and connected parking assistance system. The objective of this project is dedicated to the use of an automatic car entry/exit control system in a parking space to improve traffic congestion in an urban area. The work consists of the design and implementation of an intelligent prototype parking space on the roadside based on consultation, guidance, comfort, time, and energy management. The second part of the design involved the "smart parking" mobile application. Its role consists of identifying the available places and then reserving one.

articleTitle: New Dynamic Matrix control for a class of switched system
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, a new approach to controlling a class of switched systems is presented. This approach can systematically handle certain switching control problems such as non-minimum phase, unknown switching sequences, and time-varying or dead modes. The Dynamic-Matrix-Control (DMC) technique has been employed to establish a multi-objective control law able to deal with generalized tracking issues. A numerical example has been used to evaluate the proposed method. The obtained results highlight the ability of the developed scheme to address the control problem presented within the framework of this paper.

articleTitle: Energy management and load forecasting in Smart grid
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Energy consumption has increased considerably over the past few decades. This expansion then suggests a future interest in the use of electricity wholesalers. Predicting energy consumption requires in this work to propose two approaches, one based on long short-term memory (LSTM) and the other based on simple RNNs based on recurrent neural networks. These models take into account electricity consumption. The modeling data are from Global Energy Forecasting 2012. To evaluate the performance of the two models, four techniques are used: MSE (Mean Squared Error), MAE (Mean Absolute Error), RMSE (Root Mean Square Error) and MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error) in order to validate the best available method

articleTitle: Modeling and state estimation of discrete event systems using Hybrid Petri Nets
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This work proposes a linear algebraic model written in the form Ax ≤ b describing the dynamic behavior of Hybrid Petri Nets (HPN). The proposed model can be simulated to analyze the time evolution of the system trajectory. A state observer written in a similar form is also used to make the state estimation of HPN. The obtained results of simulation and estimation can be compared to deduce th effectiveness of the proposed models and the quality of the estimation. The obtained model is applied to an example of Hybrid Petri Net composed of discrete places and transition and continuous places and transitions to show its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing of CMOS Operational Amplifier by an Improved Ant Colony Optimization Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The optimal design of analog integrated circuits has become more and more a difficult operation requiring a lot of time for dimensioning due to extremely large-scale integration, constraints, and strict design requirements. The Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithm is a technique that has been used successfully to achieve high performance of analog circuits and subsequently the optimal sizes of transistors for IC design. However, this technique requires a significant execution time to converge toward optimal solutions. To improve the speed of convergence and subsequently the efficiency of the algorithm, the BAcktracking Search Technique has been combined with the solution-building process of the ACO algorithm. The performances of the adopted algorithm, named BA-ACO, are highlighted through the optimal design of a two-stage CMOS operational amplifier (Op-Amp). SPICE simulation results are given to show the validity of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Gain Analysis of Prototyped Wilson Current Mirror Using Double-Gate MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This research work designs and analyses a Wilson current mirror using Double-Gate (DG) MOSFET. It is suitable for biasing and constant current generation in analog design. The current analysis has been detailed for this device. The circuit simulation was performed using an electronic device simulator. Some of the benefits of independently driven double-gate MOSFET transistors in analog design have been demonstrated in this work. It allows dynamic threshold voltage adjusting; they are naturally suited to low-voltage operation.

articleTitle: An intelligent cylindrical reflector for airborne virus detection
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In 2020, the world suffered from the COVID-19 pandemic. This situation highlighted the considerable need for systems to detect viruses quickly. Providing an accurate e-health system that detects, monitors, and controls virus spread became necessary. Countries attempt to reduce the virus's spread using basic processes such as quarantine and lockdown. Early virus detection is requested to reduce the threat and decrease the propagation of the pandemic. This paper proposes an attempt to avoid speed-up spreading based on airborne virus detection. The suggested detection based on the SiNW-FET biosensor is not approved as a standardized diagnostic test. To support the airborne detection methodology, a metasurface technology based on Reflector cylindrical antenna with a sensing unit is proposed to detect viruses. The proposal considered the propagation delays and concentration of a virus. Conducted results prove that the receiver's volume is considered a primary key to an accurate detection rather than the virus's concentration.

articleTitle: Side peak cancellation by adaptive non coherent acquisition for the Galileo E1 signal
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper we propose a new method for side peak cancellation at the acquisition stage of GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) signals based on the combination of the non-coherent integrations technique and the adaptive detection CFAR (Constant False Alarm Rate), we applied the method to the acquisition of the Galileo E1 signal in an AWGN (Additive White Gaussian Noise) channel , we developed the mathematical expressions of false alarms and detection probabilities of the proposed structure, which allowed us to analyze its performances and compare it with conventional acquisition.

articleTitle: Rehabilitation robot with a new diagnostic and control protocol
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Using a connected robot for wrist and forearm rehabilitation, a new rehabilitation system is developed. Forearm and wrist biomechanics are studied as part of a rehabilitation protocol. An integrated wrist-forearm joint mathematical model is developed and integrated into the main controller. The proposed new rehabilitation protocol is composed of three main sessions: the first is dedicated to the extraction of the passive components of the dynamic model of the wrist-forearm biomechanics while the active components are extracted in the second session. The third session consists of performing the continuous exercises using the determined dynamic model of the forearm-wrist joints taking into account the torque due to muscle fatigue. In addition to determining the wrist condition and capturing the torque produced by the robot and that provided by the patient, this protocol aims to identify the level of fatigue faced by the wrist. An EMG signal is used to estimate muscle fatigue using a fuzzy classifier designed and implemented for this purpose. The results show that the rehabilitation system developed allows a good progression of the articular amplitudes as well as the resistive-active couple.

articleTitle: Lyapunov Exponents for Further Study of the Gait Complexity of the Passive Compass-Like Biped Walker
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The compass-like bipedal walker is described as an impulsive hybrid nonlinear system and is characterized by a passive gait while descending an inclined surface. To study its passive bipedal gait, an identification of the one-periodic walk should be first carried out using the Poincaré map. Moreover, bifurcation diagrams are generally employed to investigate the steady gaits of such passive gait by varying the slope angle or other parameters, and hence to confirm the display of unexpected occurrences like chaos and bifurcations. In this work, to further analyze these complex phenomena, we employ, along with the bifurcation diagrams, the Lyapunov exponents by varying the slope angle and the lower-leg segment length. Thus, we demonstrate and confirm the presence of quasi-periodic gaits and hence the exhibition of the Neimark-Sacker bifurcation.

articleTitle: A diagnostic system for classifying and segmenting breast cancer based on ultrasound images
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Breast cancer is the most common type of cancer among women worldwide. Ultrasound is a type of imaging widely used in the diagnosis and examination of many soft tissues, including abnormalities of the breast because it offers the advantages of being real-time, portable, low-cost, and non-invasive. Ultrasounds suffer from high variability as well as speckle noise, which reduces image quality; therefore, it may be difficult for doctors to detect a cancerous cell. In this paper, we use image enhancement filters to improve image quality then we develop the U-Net model to segment ultrasound images. The accuracy reached was 0.97 and the dice coefficient was 0.95. Furthermore, we classify images as malignant or benign using various traditional techniques such as k nearest neighbors (KNN), Random Forest, Decision Tree and support vector machine (SVM). The highest rate is achieved by KNN. After the image enhancement, KNN obtained an accuracy of 0.86.

articleTitle: Implementation Efficient Oil Pipelines Leak Detection and Localization System using RTTM
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Pipelines are vastly used for the transportation of oil and different types of hydrocarbon blobs over very long distances across the world. The characteristics of the pipelines are designed to resist several environmental sever conditions to guarantee safe and reliable distribution from point of production to the depot. However, leaks in pipeline networks are one of the main causes of unnumbered losses in pipeline operators and nature. To avoid disaster and build dependable pipeline infrastructure, different leakage detection and localization techniques in pipeline systems are reviewed in this paper, and their strengths and weaknesses are explained. Performance comparison is achieved to provide a clear view to decide which method is appropriate to use. In addition, this work presents the fundamentals and application of transient model-based leak detection and localization technique for crude oil pipelines. The dynamic parameters involved in this model such as pressure, flow rate, and temperature were obtained depending on changes in the flow mechanisms along the known length of the pipeline and were used in detecting, localizing, and determining the mass leak flow rate. This model located a leak in a horizontal pipeline of length 2000 meters with a diameter of 0.6 meters. A real-Time Transient Model (RTTM) was implanted using OLGA oil pipeline simulation to obtain the dynamic parameters at the inlet and outlet of the pipeline and then processed by using oil pipeline leak detection software which succeed to determine leak rate, location, and constructing data set with the same output of leak location when compared with the simulation result.

articleTitle: Enlarging the domain of attraction in nonlinear system with input saturation
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This present work focuses on the problem of estimating the largest region of attraction of nonlinear system with saturation. This nonlinear system can be put in the form of differential algebraic representation, as well as to take in to account the presence of saturation we have used a generalized sector condition for the dead zone nonlinearity. The aims of this paper is to find the large region of attraction identified with the direct theory of Lyapunov function and for find the largess domain of attraction. We proposed to use an advanced technique of optimization JAYA which swift and precise. In this present study, we present an example for demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Fractional Order and Smith Predictor Structure – Performance Analysis for Pressure Control Process
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: There is the extensive usage of traditional integer order proportional-integral-derivative (PID) control methods in industrial control systems. Recently, there is a more focus on the researcher to explore the fractional order control method. Increased flexibility in designing of control system considering its derivative and integral terms can be provided by fractional order controller. The present study discusses the fractional-order control method's performance augmented by a Smith predictor structure for a first-order plus dead time (FOPDT) process. The performance of the controller was studied using a pilot pressure control plant under fractional order, integer order, and fractional order with a Smith predictor structure. The performance of each type is studied for the proposed process through simulation. The findings indicated better performance of fractional-order controllers with the Smith predictor structure.

articleTitle: Integrated prevention mechanism based on high level Petri nets
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Our work adresses the problem of network-controlled systems under communication constraints. For a good comprension of this type of systems we must see the communication canal like a portion of the system and not a just mean of communication. Each control loop containing a network is helpless in transmitting information without induced flaws, and to ensure the finest system conduct it is critical to adjust the control and diagnostic laws.The residual generation problem consists in constructing a device, called residual generator, making it possible to elaborate, from measured inputs and outputs, a vector of fault indicators called residual vector. it can be defined as a decision support system with a main objective which is the location of the faulty components of a process and to determine the causes. In this paper, we propose a modelisation and a diagnostic mechanism based on high level Petri nets. The target of this module is to urge the better behavior by detection and anticipation fault of sensor.

articleTitle: Taguchi optimization of electrothermal microfluidic annular biosensor for rapid SARS-CoV-2 detection
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this study, Taguchi's approach was used to optimize the performance of an electrothermal microfluidic biosensor with a new shape of the reaction surface used for the rapid detection of novel severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2. An orthogonal table L9 of four critical parameters at three levels each, namely the fluid inlet velocity, the voltage applied between the electrodes, the analyte concentration at the inlet and the constant adsorption, was designed. Signal to noise ratio (S/N) combined with analysis of variance were used to reach the optimal levels of process parameters and to demonstrate the percentage contributions of each of the four controllable parameters, in terms of improved device response time

articleTitle: A new multi-access technique OFDMA-RL for remote lab system
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The Remote Lab System (RLS) is a special combination between software and materials to give the chance for students to access remotely the laboratory equipment. With this system universities will be able to build a full online license and master's degree. Actually, the operational remote lab allows students access the equipment remotely. The number of beneficiaries of remote lab services continues to increase. The reservation process and the limit of the slot time given for each student became weaknesses for the RLS. In this paper, we propose and test a famous technique to share remotely the laboratory equipment between students at the same time. In fact, we test the Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiple Access (OFDMA) and exploit the good user separation done by the OFDMA technique, and also each users is assigned a frequency. The identification of each user or equipment lab will be based on the assigned frequency. Applying OFDMA to manage multi- user of our RLS allows us more than one student access our equipment lab. The system OFDMA allows students reused some equipment lab in multiple practical work or shared it between multiple-users. The limitation of our software and equipment lab present a hard barrier for us to test our solution for more than three users at the same time. In order to let our system stable we decide to give the possibility for only two users sharing the laboratory equipment at the same time.

articleTitle: Multi-parameter Sensing Based on the Stimulated Brillouin Scattering in Ring Core Fibers
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, we designed two ring core fibers (RCFs) for the simultaneous sensing of temperature and strain using stimulated Brillouin scattering. The designed fibers are referred to as step index RCF (SI-RCF) and graded index RCF (GI-RCF). Numerical simulations proved that the designed RCFs achieve temperature sensitivities of 1.928 MHz/°C for SI-RCF and 1.872 MHz/°C for GI-RCF, and strain sensitivities of 0.087 MHz/με for SI-RCF and 0.0842 MHz/με for GI-RCF. The respective optimal errors for the simultaneous sensing of temperature and strain have been evaluated and discussed for both designed RCFs. The reported results and the performed comparisons with literature confirm that the designed RCFs sensors could find applications in next generation Brillouin sensing systems for enabling temperature and strain discrimination.

articleTitle: Optimization of a Permanent Magnet Motor with Firefly Metaheuristic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In recent years, permanent magnet machines have been widely used in various industrial applications especially in electric vehicles. This is due to their high torque density, power density, and efficiency. Among these machines, the surface mounted permanent magnet machine has proven its presence in this field. Due to the complex magnetic circuit of this machines and to find the optimum machine dimensions an optimization procedure must performed. The objective of this paper is the implementation of the Firefly algorithm (FA) for the optimization of a permanent magnet machine intended for an electric vehicle application. At first, and to find the optimum motor design, a metaheuristic method, based on the FA is applied. Two objective functions are used: the efficiency maximization and the weight minimization. Then an optimized machine is investigated by finite element analysis (FEA).

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Smart Pill Box for Healthcare Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The main objective of this research is to facilitate the old people daily life, who suffer from one or more chronic diseases and who have to take dozens of pills a day, by reminding them to take each pill in the time suggested by the doctor. In fact, this paper presents a smart pill box composed of an arduino MEGA 2560R3, a LCD display with I2C module, a DHT22 temperature and humidity and a MQ-4 gas sensors, a buzzer and a wifi module ESP8266. Using the IoT (Internet of Things) technology, the proposed pill box is controlled by a mobile application allowing the remote monitoring of data storage and real-time display for the patient himself and for the doctor who will be able to access to the cloud in order to also display in time if the patient has taken his medicine. Then, the doctor or the patient's relatives are informed by sms or an email when the patient has not taken his treatment.

articleTitle: Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm for EIT Image Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) is a clinical imaging technique that gained a lot of attention because it is a non-invasive and radiation-free method. To obtain an inner image of the domain under study, a specific number of electrodes is attached to the surface of the object, then through a pair of electrodes, a low alternative current is injected. Potentials produced by this injection are measured with the remaining electrodes. Based on these boundary voltages measurements, the inner conductivity can be inferred, thus the image is reconstructed. The focus of this paper is to overcome the major weakness of the EIT image reconstruction technique, which is the low spatial resolution of the reconstructed images caused by the non-linearity of EIT inverse problem. This paper considers this problem, an optimization problem that is solved using the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) meta-heuristic. A variant of the standard PSO is proposed and validated, first on a circular mesh composed of 686 triangles then on a lung mesh composed of 2707 triangles.

articleTitle: Synchronverter as Control Strategy of Grid-Forming Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The power grid is currently experiencing a significant transition from centralized to distributed generation along with high penetration of inverter-based electrical systems. Inverters, providing auxiliary services, can be referred to smart inverters like grid-forming inverters and specifically the synchronverter. In the islanding mode, the synchronverter forms the grid by determining the voltage profile and supplying active and reactive power for frequency and voltage control. As such, the synchronverter can be described as a controlled inverter that operates like Synchronous Generator (SG). In this paper, the synchronverter general and technical overview are presented with the simulation results to validate the model’s performance.

articleTitle: A Modified DBSCAN clustering algorithm for the identification of PWA systems
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of identifying hybrid systems of class PWARX (PriceWise Auto-Regressive with Exogenous Inputs) based on the classification technique. This approach is insured by three main steps namely; data clustering, parameters vector estimation and regions estimation. This work is devoted to the data clustering step based on the DBSCAN (Density Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise) clustering technique which has the ability to eliminate outliers and can group classes with arbitrary shapes. However, the performance of the DBSCAN algorithm degrades with dense adjacent clusters. Therefore, we have proposed an improvement of this algorithm. The simulation and experimental results show the efficiency and performance of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Structural Holding Monitoring and Microclimate Measurements in Museum Showcases
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The study under consideration in this paper, focuses on microclimatic monitoring of physical quantities of interest in order to preserves the painting "Portrait of a Gentleman" (1570), restored in 2018 and attributed to El Greco, located inside the Civic Museum of Catania, Castello Ursino in Italy. Particular emphasis has been given to measurement of relative humidity, temperature and vibrations inside the theca where the artwork is placed. An IoT system, with vibrational transducers, a wireless transmission and data management has been used in order to demonstrate the suitability of the proposed device for cultural heritage applications.

articleTitle: An Effective Random Forest based Long-Term Wind Power Forecasting Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Accurate Wind Power Forecasting (WPF) has become an essential task for grid operators due to its ability to minimize the effect of wind power intermittency and the need of energy storage deployment. In this paper, a Random Forest (RF)-based long-term WPF technique is proposed. The model inputs consist of some meteorological parameters such as wind speed, temperature, and pressure. The input data are selected from the data NOAA’S Surface Radiation (SURFRAD) network at Bondville station (USA). The RF parameters (number of trees, number of leaves) are optimized to get the best prediction accuracy. The normalized RMSE and MAE metrics are computed to assess the performance of the proposed RF model.

articleTitle: Hybrid Wheelchair control method with EEG signal and facial Expression
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: While degrading their mobility, one of the major concerns of elderly/disabled people is affecting their ability to live independently. Assistive technologies for mobility are now designed to improve people’s living conditions. However, improvements are needed to existing mobility assist devices. This article explores the design and control of a smart wheelchair with two sources of control to improve wheelchair user safety. To improve user involvement and safety, the proposed system includes control interfaces with the EEG signal processing application using the EMOTIV Insight EEG headset in addition to facial expressions using a webcam, at the same time defining the state of the user.

articleTitle: Design of Novel Reciprocal Inverse Graded Index Fiber (R-IGIF) For OAM-SDM communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: in this paper, we harness the duality between the convexity and the concavity of refractive index (RI) profile in order to design novel RI for optical communication that we refer to as the reciprocal-inverse graded index fiber (R-IGIF). Numerical simulations, using finite element method, have been carried out targeting to assess the performances metrics/transmission features of the designed fiber. The latter include the supported OAM channels, the separation between them, the chromatic dispersion, the differential group delay and the resilience in practical environment such as the bending. The obtained results, the performed discussions and the conducted comparisons with recently reported fibers confirm the viability/appropriateness of the designed fiber in next generation SDM communication systems and networks.

articleTitle: Voltage Balancing Using Particle Swarm Optimization and Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) are proposed in this paper to provide an intelligent integrated solution for controlling reactive power and restoring voltage balance in a three-phase power system. The PSO algorithm is used in offline mode to determine the optimal set of firing angles for the Thyristor-Controlled-Reactor compensator according to the smallest fitness value required for voltage balancing. SVM are presented as online mode controllers for quickly and precisely restoring voltage balance. The optimum firing angles obtained by PSO are used to train the SVM. The SVM models are finally used as real-time controllers to retrieve the voltage balance in online mode. A simulation model and experimental setup of the electrical power system are built. Several simulations and practical case studies have been conducted to test and validate the capability of the proposed approach in solving the voltage unbalance problem. The results indicated the proposed approach’s superior capacity to restore voltage balance rapidly.

articleTitle: Energy Efficient Wake-up Receiver MAC Protocol in OMNeT++ for Indoor Wireless Sensor Network Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: A wireless sensor network is composed of a large number of spatially distributed wireless sensor nodes that communicate with each other over a long duration to collect the maximum data accumulated from the physical environment. To accomplish such a mission wireless sensor nodes are usually equipped with a radio transceiver, micro-controller, a set of sensors, and a battery, Power efficiency is required in power-limited wireless sensor networks. Numerous studies have proven that the receiving mode in the radio transceiver is the most consuming process when collecting data, as a result, the wake-up receiver(WuRx) gains much interest due to the low power consumption. The contribution of this paper is the implementation of a wake-up radio mac-based protocol(WUR-MAC) in OMNeT++ to investigate the energy efficiency of WuRx that include a low-frequency pattern matcher(LFPMs) such as the AS3933. Performance comparison of the implemented mac-based protocol(WUR-MAC) with duty-cycled MAC protocol is explored.

articleTitle: A new design of a bionic hand controlled by EMG signals : A preliminary study
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: A bionic hand might provide a good replacement for the human hand when carrying out various tasks. In recent years, hand movements have been widely recognized via myoelectric control. Although a few research has looked at the hand-grip position, the majority of earlier investigations have concentrated on whole-hand movements.
